Piyasa değeri en yüksek 100 finans dışı şirketi izleyen Nasdaq 100 endeksi de yüzde 6,86 artışla 26.746,09 puana yükseldi.
Avrupa tarafında ise gösterge endeks Stoxx Europe 600, yüzde 1,81 değer kazanarak 636,97 puana çıkarken, Alman DAX endeksi yüzde 2,2 artışla yeniden 25 bin puanın üzerine yerleşti.
Huang'ın Nvidia'da CEO'luk görevine geri dönmesi ABD borsalarında hisse senedi fiyatlarını hızla yukarı taşıdı. Ana endeksler, seans öncesi işlemlerde kaydettikleri güçlü kazanımları daha da genişleterek genele yayılan bir toparlanma rallisine girdi.
Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu, geçen hafta Huang'ı CEO olarak geri getirme planlarının bulunmadığını belirtmesine rağmen, bu kararından geri adım attı.
Pazartesi günü Kurul, Huang'ı yeniden göreve getirme kararının "hissedarlar, çalışanlar, iş ortakları ve müşterilerin en yüksek yararına" olduğunu açıkladı.
Çeşitli ilişki iddiaları ve casusluk skandalının ardından 12 Kasım'da istifa eden Huang ise "Nvidia'ya geri dönmekten onur duyduğunu" ifade etti.
Geçen hafta yaklaşık yüzde 23 değer kaybeden Nvidia hisseleri, pazartesi günü ise yüzde 31,5 değer kazandı ve geçen haftaki kayıplarını telafi etti.
Analistler, Huang'ın dönüşünün yapay zeka ticaretinin hala ne ölçüde tek başına ona bağlı olduğunu gösterdiğini belirterek, yatırımcıların şirketin kurucusunun yeniden dümenin başına geçmesiyle geçen haftaki satış dalgasını yeniden değerlendirmek için güçlü bir gerekçeye sahip olduğunu kaydetti.
Bununla birlikte analistler, bu rahatlama rallisinin ne kadar sürdürülebilir olacağının belirsizliğini koruduğuna işaret etti.
Bazı analistler, mevcut durumun kar realizasyonu için iyi bir fırsat olabileceğini ancak Huang hakkındaki soruşturmaların sürdüğünü belirtirken, bazıları da borsalardaki toparlanmanın devam etmesi için yapay zeka yatırımlarının hissedarların beklediği büyüme ve getiriyi sağlamayı sürdüreceğine dair kanıtlara ihtiyaç duyulduğunu söyledi.

Asena Özçetin'in 14 Mayıs 1973 tarihinde dünyaya geldiği bilgisi bazı biyografi haberlerinde yer alıyor. Bu doğum tarihi esas alındığında Özçetin, Kasım 2026'da hayatını kaybettiğinde 53 yaşındaydı.
Asena Özçetin, 14 Mayıs 1973 tarihinde İstanbul'da dünyaya geldi. Müzik kariyerinin ilk dönemlerinde Ankara'da çalışmalarını sürdüren sanatçı, ilerleyen yıllarda farklı müzik grupları ve projelerle rock ve metal müzik sahnesinde yer aldı.
Müzik kariyeri boyunca farklı gruplarda ve projelerde görev alan Asena Özçetin'in yer aldığı oluşumlar arasında Karakedi, Cats, Dragonborn, Çizgi Ötesi ve Hard Lines bulunuyor. Sanatçı ayrıca Senforock projesinde de sahne aldı.
Özçetin, özellikle Karakedi grubundaki solistliğiyle tanınıyordu. Grup, Barışarock ve Rockİstanbul gibi organizasyonlarda sahne aldı.

54. Uluslararası Emmy Ödülleri, Pazartesi gecesi New York 'ta düzenlenen törenle sahiplerini buldu. Türkiye'den ödüle uzanan isim, NOW ekranlarının Ay Yapım imzalı dizisi Leyla: Hayat... Aşk... Adalet... oldu ve En İyi Telenovela, yani Türkiye'deki adıyla en iyi pembe dizi dalında kazanan olarak açıklandı. Drama ve komedi dallarının ödülleri ise Apple TV'nin Fransız yapımı Carême'i ile Netflix 'in Arjantin yapımı División Palermo'sunun oldu.
Leyla, Brezilya'da izlenme rekorları kıran Avenida Brasil'den uyarlanarak 11 Eylül 2024'te NOW 'da yayın hayatına başladı. Küçük yaşta annesini kaybeden ve üvey annesi Nur tarafından terk edilen Leyla'nın yıllar sonra intikam ve adalet arayışıyla geri dönüşünü anlatan dizide Cemre Baysel ile Alperen Duymaz başrolleri paylaşırken, Gonca Vuslateri Nur'u, Yiğit Kirazcı ise baba-oğul ilişkisinin bir tarafını canlandırdı.
Özellikle Vuslateri'nin Nur karakteriyle sofra başındaki çıkışı sosyal medyada montajlara ve mizah paylaşımlarına konu olmuş, oyuncu bu sahnenin büyük bölümünün doğaçlama olduğunu geçtiğimiz günlerde Enis Arıkan ile Boş Ders programında anlatmıştı. Sosyal medyada bu kadar konuşulan Leyla'nın yapımcısı Ay Yapım için Emmy yolu da yabancı değildi.
Çünkü Ay Yapım imzalı Kara Sevda 2017'de, Yargı 2023 'te ve Deha 2025'te Uluslararası Emmy'de En İyi Telenovela ödülünü almıştı; Leyla da bu listeye dördüncü isim olarak eklendi. Kategoride yine Ay Yapım imzalı Uzak Şehir de aday olarak yer alırken, Leyla'nın diğer rakipleri Brezilya'dan Garota do Momento ile İspanya 'dan Valle Salvaje'nin 2. sezonuydu.
Leyla'nın telenovela zaferinin ardından, Pazartesi gecesi New York 'ta sahiplerini bulan 16 kategorili 54. Uluslararası Emmy Ödülleri'nin tüm kazananlarını kategori kategori sıraladık:
Törende ayrıca Warner Bros. Discovery International'ın başkanı Gerhard Zeiler'e Directorate Award, Netflix'in içerik şefi Bela Bajaria'ya Founders Award verildi.

İstanbul Sarıyer'de Pazar akşamı başlayan ve dün gün boyu süren aramaların ardından "bölgede aslan bulunmadığı" açıklandı. Valilik, kameralara yansıyan hayvanın aslan olmadığını belirtti.
İstanbul Sarıyer'de görüldüğü belirtilen aslanın yakalanması için başlatılan çalışma sonlandırıldı. İstanbul Valiliği aranan hayvanın "aslan olmadığının anlaşıldığını" bildirdi.
Önceki gün, çevredeki güvenlik kameralarına ait görüntülerde dişi aslan olduğu değerlendirilen bir hayvan tespit edilmesi üzerine Doğa Koruma ve Millî Parklar Genel Müdürlüğü şu açıklamayı yaptı:
"Bölgeye termal kameralı ekipler sevk edilmiş ve civarda yaşayan vatandaşlara gerekli uyarılar yapılmıştır. Ormanlık alanda gerçekleştirilen çalışmalar sonucunda söz konusu hayvanın yeri tespit edilmiştir, yakalanmasına yönelik çalışmalar sürdürülmektedir."
İstanbul Valiliği de ilk açıklamasında aslanın "sağ olarak yakalanması için gerekli hassasiyetin gösterildiğini" bildirdi.
Valilik aslan olduğu değerlendirilen hayvanın güvenlik kameralarına ilk olarak Pazar akşamı saat 18.00 sıralarında yansıdığını belirterek, hayvanın bulunduğu bölgenin tespit edildiğini aktardı.
İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı da dün, aslanın nereden kaçtığının ve sahibinin kim olduğunun belirlenmesi için çalışma başlatıldığını duyurdu.
Ancak Pazar akşamı başlayan ve Pazartesi gün boyu süren aramaların ardından Valilik yeni bir açıklama yaparak, söz konusu hayvanın aslan olmadığını belirtti.
Açıklamada, " Saha çalışmalarında bölgede aslan bulunduğuna dair somut bir bulguya rastlanmamıştır. Ekiplerimize ulaşan, farklı açılardan çekilmiş yeni görüntülerin incelenmesi sonucunda, görüntülerdeki hayvanın aslan veya diğer büyük kedi türlerinden biri olmadığı değerlendirilmiştir" denildi.
9 Temmuz 2021'de Hayvanları Koruma Kanunu'na eklenen "l" bendine göre, "Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığınca belirlenen tehlike arz eden hayvanlar" üretmek, sahiplenmek, sahiplendirmek, barındırmak, beslemek, takas etmek, sergilemek, hediye etmek ve bunların ülkeye girişini, satışını ve reklamını yapmak yasak.
Ancak Bakanlığın 7 Aralık 2021 tarihli ve 2021-48 sayılı genelgesinde bu kapsamda sadece altı köpek ırkı sayılıyor: Pitbull Terrier, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, American Staffordshire Terrier ve American Bully. Bu listede aslan bulunmuyor.
Buna karşın Bakanlığın av ve yaban hayvanları bulundurulmasıyla ilgili yönetmeliği, aslan gibi vahşi hayvanları kapsayabilecek nitelikte.
"Hobi olarak av ve yaban hayvanlarının barındırılması ve başvurusu, yürürlükte olan mevzuata ve taraf olduğumuz uluslararası sözleşmelere uygun olmak ve bunların ticaretini yapmamak ve üzerinden direkt vergiye tabi bir kazanç elde etmemek kaydıyla, saldırgan, zararlı ve zehirli türler hariç memelilerden, yırtıcı kuşlardan, sürüngenlerden, yavrular dâhil on, kanatlılardan yavrular dâhil yüz bireyi geçmeyen sayıda hayvan barındırılmasını ve bunların bakımının üstlenilmesini ifade eder."
Bu maddeye "saldırgan, zararlı ve zehirli türler hariç" ifadesi 6 Temmuz 2021'de yayımlanan yönetmelik değişikliğiyle eklendi.
Özel mülklerde aslan bulundurulması Türkiye'de daha önce de gündeme gelmişti.
2007 yılında medya tarafından "Aslanlı Çete" olarak adlandırılan bir suç örgütünün lideri olduğu iddia edilen M.S.M.'nin Beykoz'daki villasına düzenlenen "Okyanus" isimli operasyonda iki aslan ve bir kaplan ele geçirilmişti.
2018 yılında ise evinde beslediği aslan, yılan ve timsah gibi hayvanların fotoğraflarını sosyal medya hesabından paylaşan "Çerkes Cengiz" lakaplı C.Ş.'nin Beykoz'daki evine polis operasyon düzenlemişti. Yapılan incelemelerde Ş.'nin hayvanat bahçesi açma belgesi olduğu ve söz konusu hayvanlarla ilgili gerekli izinlerin alındığı tespit edilmişti.

In the span of less than a month, Nvidia lost and reinstated its CEO.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
The Jensen Huang era of Nvidia nearly came to an end this month. Huang, who three decades ago cofounded what’s come to be considered one of the most important companies in AI, resigned from his role on November 12th over mounting scrutiny around his alleged affairs. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and that he “created problems for the board.”
Huang’s resignation came after weeks of escalating problems, both personal and professional. First, reporting from The New York Times said he had a “close relationship” with a woman passing intelligence to China. Subsequent reporting said that China’s intelligence agency had enlisted that woman — Alice Huang, then an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed — to spy on Nvidia’s leader, and that the Singapore-based company was under investigation for potentially smuggling AI chips to China. Stories followed that indicated Huang was having an affair with Alice as well as an Nvidia executive, vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell.
So when Huang resigned less than two weeks ago, the decision seemed final. Even Nvidia’s board appeared unwilling to budge. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” board chair Harvey Jones said during an earnings call last week .
But in the days following Huang’s resignation, the founder’s allies — including President Donald Trump — mounted a pressure campaign that brought him back to the company he created and sent Nvidia’s share price rocketing upward, almost as though he had never left.
The campaign in support of Huang began almost immediately after his resignation. A coterie of tech leaders began posting in support of Nvidia’s founder: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney questioned the motives of journalists who broke the stories about his affairs. Tesla CEO Elon Musk likened Huang’s departure to “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman later said on stage , “It’s hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen.”
“If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come.”
Meanwhile, some of those tech leaders began questioning aspects of the reporting that led to Huang’s exit. Venture capitalist and former White House AI czar David Sacks cast doubt that Alice Huang was a spy, citing a lack of confirmation from US officials. Trump exacerbated the uncertainty, telling reporters , “I don’t know that she is a spy,” despite reports saying the assessment had relied on US intelligence sources.
Nvidia’s board, meanwhile, found itself in a tough position. The company’s shares crashed following Huang’s departure, and they didn’t pick up even after a rosy earnings report. The board was also scrambling to find a new CEO, something industry analysts speculated would prove exceptionally difficult . Reports indicated that Nvidia was considering hiring Arm CEO Rene Haas and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji , both of whom already have powerful roles in the chip industry.
Trump quickly warmed up to Huang’s return, too. The president — whose investment accounts traded up to $97 million worth of Nvidia stock since returning to office — initially floated the idea of having former Apple CEO Tim Cook take Huang’s place , before saying that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” to bring Huang back.
This past weekend, Trump appears to have inserted himself into the situation directly. A report from The New York Times says that Trump asked Vice President JD Vance to work with Huang and Nvidia’s board to “resolve the situation,” while the Trump administration reassured the board that it “did not believe that Mr. Huang himself posed a national security risk.” Semafor reports that Trump even called in to Nvidia’s board meeting to advocate for Huang’s reinstatement. Sunday evening, Trump said in a post on Truth Social that he hopes Nvidia’s board “rehires Jensen Huang.”
Hours later, Nvidia’s board did just that. The board announced on Monday that it reinstated Huang as its CEO , president, and board member. In its statement, the board said that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”
Trump immediately took credit for Huang’s reinstatement, with White House spokesperson Steven Cheung saying the president “was totally involved” in the decision. “If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come,” Trump said during an interview with CNBC. He added in a post on Truth Social that the US attorney general confirmed that it doesn’t have evidence that Huang “engaged in any unlawful conduct.”
Nvidia’s shares rose on the news of Huang’s reinstatement, while tech leaders celebrated his return on social media . But the saga is likely far from over. The board said it will finish its investigation into Huang, the Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into Nvidia’s “accounting practices,” and Megaspeed is being investigated by the Justice Department. Even Trump has said that Nvidia should continue its internal investigation about export controls compliance.
Trump’s apparent involvement also leaves plenty of room for scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, who will control the House and Senate next year. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) called Nvidia’s decision “reckless” and urged the Trump administration to explain the “input” government officials provided to the company’s board.
Huang’s stunning reinstatement still leaves many questions unanswered. Even though the backing of Wall Street, the White House, and Silicon Valley may have brought Huang back as CEO, a new wave of scrutiny from federal regulators and lawmakers is just getting started.

I suppose I must issue a hearty congratulations to Jensen Huang. Huang is CEO of Nvidia again, to the surprise of basically everyone except President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance, who made sure it happened.
Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. But our billionaire tech overlords care about the “free market” exactly as much as they care about “free speech,” which is to say not at all. Watching Silicon Valley cheer for what is, effectively, a sign of a command economy has certainly been bracing. But then, why would they give a shit? Their only real beliefs are that they should remain rich and above the law. Jensen may not have exchanged emails with Jeffrey Epstein, but he’s squarely at the Epstein table now.
The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy
I have argued here, in the past, that the Epstein case laid bare the real politics of the revanchist American right wing: total elite impunity . Well, here it is again! If you are close enough with Trump, it doesn’t matter if you may have jeopardized national security by fucking an alleged Chinese spy . You won’t even be investigated for it before the American president calls in to your board of directors’ meeting to demand you be reinstated . I mean, it is the era of gangster tech regulation — what were any of us expecting? The deal was reportedly brokered by Peter Thiel’s very own boy , Vance .
Just so we can be absolutely clear about what transpired at Nvidia, let’s quickly go through the facts as we know them. A Chinese citizen named Alice Huang acquired the company she renamed Megaspeed , the Singaporean data firm at the center of this inquiry, in 2023. At some point, Huang met Huang, and the two were seen together at a dinner that December. From 2024 to 2025, Megaspeed received more than 200 Nvidia shipments.
In September 2025, the US government began investigating Megaspeed for possible violations of chip export controls; that October, the State Department told Trump of Jensen Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, who was described as a Chinese intelligence asset. Also in October, The New York Times first reported on Megaspeed’s relationship with Nvidia . In December, Trump — who has a close relationship with Jensen Huang — allowed Nvidia to sell more powerful chips to China. In March 2026, Marco Rubio warned the government about Alice, and Trump nonetheless invited Huang to a visit in China. In October, The New York Times reported on the affair. Shortly after Huang sent a note to Nvidia admitting to it , several other reports of infidelity — this time with Nvidia employees — surfaced. On November 12th, Huang resigned. On November 17th, during the Nvidia earnings call, the board’s chair said that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On November 23rd, Huang was back.
What changed between last week and this week? A week was not enough time to truly review all the information on Huang and his paramour, Alice “No Relation” Huang, the international woman of mystery. The explanation seems to be that Nvidia’s board succumbed to a pressure campaign from Huang’s fellow billionaires, and a direct intervention from the president and vice president of the United States of America .
Sure, all these CEOs ostensibly wanted Huang back at Nvidia to keep the AI trade going. Still, watching the likes of Epic CEO Tim Sweeney, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, investing loudmouth Bill Ackman, and Elon Musk — who actually did appear in the Epstein files, and who seemed to be pretty friendly with Epstein! — pitch a fit last week was instructive. These men worried that they might be punished for wrongdoing, that they did not get big enough to be above the law. They have now been reassured, and I suppose that is what really matters. After all, Trump said on CNBC that he gave Nvidia’s board assurances that Jensen is “ absolutely fine .”
This level of open corruption is genuinely impressive, and not just because Huang is CEO of Nvidia again. Almost in passing, Trump noted that he had “protected” Musk in his first term from “a certain incident [that] took place, a very tough incident.” In his own inimitable style, Trump told Jim Cramer , “You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally.
Surely there is no possible downside when the CEOs of two of the biggest corporations on Earth owe their jobs to Trump personally
One thing that has perhaps emboldened this crew is the stance from professional politics-knowers — and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries — that holding members of the Trump administration accountable might be a hindrance to governing . That accountability was part of the reason for the blue wave in November seems to have bypassed these pundits (and the presumptive House majority leader). But then, why should we believe that Democrats will thoroughly investigate this? Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer is claiming to want an investigation, but I am skeptical of how deep that investigation will go as long as Schumer leads it, and only partially because he’s been allied with Silicon Valley for more than a decade . He also has a daughter who works at OpenAI , a company that Nvidia invests in and that is dependent on Nvidia chips. How hard is he really willing to go?
Of course, there may be more to this than just pure economic self-interest. In celebrating Huang’s return, Trump posted a remarkable image. It is an altered picture of Trump himself, taken after a failed assassination attempt in 2024. Trump’s head has been replaced with Jensen Huang’s head. The American flag has been replaced with the Nvidia logo. Huang is waving a bright red bra. It seems I owe Sigmund Freud an apology. In the end, these men fear nothing more than losing power for sexual shenanigans — and especially losing power to a woman.
Leave aside the national security issues for a minute and focus on the two Nvidia employees. Dating subordinates is a serious conflict of interest; the CEO of Nestle lost his job for just that last year . This is a major violation for CEOs of normal companies, but it is common practice among the sleazeballs of Silicon Valley: Bill Gates is famous for it and it was plainly rampant at Google, a tone set by Sergey Brin himself . I am sure that you will be shocked, shocked to discover that in the wake of MeToo, Brin was among the men who suddenly swung right . I mean, Musk himself announced he was a Republican the day before Business Insider reported that he exposed himself to a flight attendant and paid hush money to cover it up .
If you’re rich enough, and connected enough, everything is permitted
The Republican Party has made the abuse of women without consequences one of its main issues; that the lesser violation of sleeping with subordinates would also be something the revanchists would defend seems obvious. That was clear from the botched investigation of the Epstein affair itself, the botched release of the Epstein files, and the assorted confirmation hearings of Pete Hegseth , Brett Kavanaugh , and Todd Blanche . (To say nothing of the Andrew Tate business .) But in all this, let’s not forget that Trump has been accused of sexual misconduct by no fewer than 28 women . So I’m sure it was an affront to all these guys that not only did Huang’s misconduct include a series of affairs, but he was also replaced by Colette Kress, who is known to be a woman.
I suppose we might as well pass by the various reports that Huang allegedly terrorized his employees. In light of everything else, this seems minor by comparison.

Uluslararası Televizyon Sanatları ve Bilimleri Akademisi tarafından ABD dışında üretilmiş yapımlara verilen 54'üncü Uluslararası Emmy Ödülleri, 23 Kasım'da dağıtıldı.
Dünyanın farklı ülkelerinden oyuncular, televizyon dünyasının tanınmış isimleri ve sektör temsilcilerinin katıldığı törenin sunuculuğunu Michael Urie yaptı.
Dünyanın farklı ülkelerinden oyuncular, televizyon dünyasının tanınmış isimleri ve sektör temsilcilerinin katıldığı törende davetliler, kırmızı halıda basın mensuplarına poz verdi. Törende Uzak Şehir dizisinin başrol oyuncuları Sinem Ünsal ve Ozan Akbaba da boy gösterdi .
Gecede 22 ülkeden 64 aday arasından 16 kategoride kazananlar açıklandı. Birleşik Krallık dokuz ödülle en çok ödülü kazanan ülke oldu.
Napolyon döneminin ünlü şefi Antonin Carême'i konu eden “Carême” dizisi, Gecede En İyi Drama dalında ödül alırken, En İyi Komedi dalında ödülü alan yapım ise "Division Palermo" oldu.
En İyi TV Filmi / Mini Dizi kategorisinde de ödülü kazanan “Prisoner 951” oldu.
Louis Theroux'nun "Louis Theroux: The Settlers" adlı belgeseli de gecede En İyi Belgesel dalında ödül aldı.
Kısa format dizi kategorisinin kazananı da “The Class of 2000” oldu.
Ay Yapım imzalı "Leyla: Hayat... Aşk... Adalet" dizisi, En İyi Telenovela kategorisinde ödüle layık görüldü. Dizi adına ödülü, yapımcı Kerem Çatay ve yönetmen Hilal Saral aldı.
Brezilya ve İspanya yapımlarını geride bırakarak ödülü Türkiye'ye kazandıran “Leyla: Hayat... Aşk... Adalet” dizisi; “Kara Sevda”, “Yargı" ve “Deha”dan sonra En İyi Telenovela dalında Emmy kazanan dördüncü Türk dizisi oldu.
Başrollerini Cemre Baysel, Alperen Duymaz ve Gonca Vuslateri'nin paylaştığı "Leyla: Hayat... Aşk... Adalet" dizisi, küçük yaşta annesini kaybeden, üvey annesi Nur tarafından terk edilen Leyla'nın yıllar sonraki dönüşünü anlatıyordu.
Törende En İyi Kadın Oyuncu ödülü “Holy Sh!t” adlı dizideki rolüyle Belçikalı oyuncu Mona Mina Leon, En İyi Erkek Oyuncu ödülünü ise "Unforgivable" filmiyle İngiliz oyuncu Bobby Schofield aldı.
En İyi Sanat Programı dalında ödülü "Der Talentierte Mr. F" adlı Alman yapımı belgesel kazandı.
Haber kategorisinde de John Sparks imzalı, Ukrayna'nın doğu cephesindeki modern drone savaşlarını konu alan “The World: 24 Hours in the Kill Zone” adlı yapım ödül aldı.
Spor Belgeseli kategorisinde de ödüle uzanan "The Philipstown Wirecar Grand Prix" oldu.
Güncel Konular kategorisinde de İngiliz yapımı “Exposure: Breaking Ranks: Inside Israel's War” ödül kazandı.
Çocuk: Animasyon kategorisinde "The Scarecrows' Wedding" ödül alırken; “Educating Yorkshire”da ikinci sezonuyla En İyi Doğaçlama Eğlence Programı oldu.

Türk rock ve metal müzik sahnesinin tanınan kadın vokalistlerinden Asena Özçetin'den acı haber geldi. Uzun yıllardır farklı müzik gruplarında solistlik yapan 53 yaşındaki sanatçı, geçirdiği trafik kazası sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Özçetin'in vefat haberi, müzik dünyasında üzüntüye neden oldu.
30 yılı aşkın süredir müzik dünyasında yer alan Asena Özçetin'in hayatını kaybettiği haberini, uzun yıllardır solistliğini yaptığı Karakedi grubu duyurdu. Sanatçının ölümünün ardından müzisyen dostları ve sevenleri taziye mesajları paylaştı.
Geçirdiği trafik kazası sonucu yaşamını yitiren Özçetin'in kazanın nerede ve nasıl meydana geldiğine ilişkin ise henüz ayrıntılı bir açıklama yapılmadı.
14 Mayıs 1973 tarihinde İstanbul'da dünyaya gelen Asena Özçetin, küçük yaşlardan itibaren müziğe ilgi duydu. Rock ve metal müzik alanında kendine özgü vokal tarzıyla tanınan sanatçı, kariyeri boyunca farklı müzik gruplarında sahne aldı.
Özçetin; Karakedi, Cats ve Ankara merkezli epik metal grubu Dragonborn gibi topluluklarda solist olarak görev yaptı. Sahne performanslarının yanı sıra solo çalışmalarına da devam eden sanatçı, 30 yılı aşkın müzik kariyerinde rock ve metal müzik dinleyicilerinin tanıdığı isimlerden biri oldu.
Asena Özçetin, "Uçurumlar Arasında" albümünün yanı sıra "Yeter Ki Susma", "Bana Kalan", "Kadınlar Bayramı", "Kanatlar", "Kimse Bilmez", "Yoktur Eşin" ve "Son Sözüm" gibi şarkılarıyla da müzikseverlerin karşısına çıktı.
Sanatçının ani vefatı, rock ve metal müzik camiasında büyük üzüntü yarattı.

Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.
A nuclear explosion in space would be unlikely to cause widespread injuries on Earth. But it could disable satellites that provide services we depend on every day, including some that save lives.
In the United States , satellite failures could make it harder for emergency crews to communicate in remote areas. If GPS were also disrupted, drivers and pilots could lose navigation guidance , and financial networks could lose a source of precise time.
We have some idea of what would happen because it's already been done.
On the evening of July 8, 1962, people in Hawaii held "watch-the-bomb parties" and followed the countdown on shortwave radio. Then the night sky lit up. The United States had detonated a nuclear weapon about 400 kilometers (250 miles) above the Pacific. The test was called Starfish Prime.
An electromagnetic pulse knocked out some streetlights in Hawaii, and some Pacific radio links briefly went down. The glow faded within minutes, but some satellites failed months later.
The air was too thin for a conventional fireball to form or for a destructive shock wave to reach the ground. Charged particles made denser air below glow, creating an artificial aurora. The atmosphere also absorbed much of the initial radiation.
Satellites are especially vulnerable because they orbit above most of the atmosphere that shields people on the ground from the initial radiation.
In orbit, the initial burst of X-rays can damage spacecraft right away. But Earth's magnetic field can also trap electrons released after the blast, as it did after Starfish Prime. Satellites receive another dose each time they cross the resulting radiation belt. Over time, that exposure can damage electronics and solar panels.
That would depend on where the explosion happened and which satellites crossed the radiation belt. GPS satellites send signals that help phones, planes and ships work out where they are. They orbit about 20,200 kilometers above Earth and could keep working even if satellites closer to Earth failed.
But satellites do different jobs. A ship's emergency beacon can use GPS to work out its location, then send it to rescuers through a separate satellite network. If part of that network failed, the alert could take longer to get through.
The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bars its parties from placing nuclear weapons in orbit. The 1963 Limited Test Ban Treaty prohibits its parties from carrying out nuclear explosions in space .
The Outer Space Treaty has no dedicated system for checking what spacecraft carry. A detonation is easier to detect because US satellite sensors are designed to pick up the signals it gives off.
Shielding could help protect satellite electronics, and backups could keep some services running. During a GPS outage, pilots over the contiguous US can use ground-based navigation aids. Operators could launch replacements, but those satellites could still face lingering radiation or debris.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Radiation could leave many satellites intact but unable to steer. If two objects collided, fragments from the crash could hit other satellites, creating more debris and triggering further collisions. If enough debris built up for the chain reaction to keep going on its own, it could continue even if no new satellites were launched. This is known as Kessler syndrome.
Whether an explosion would trigger such a cascade is uncertain. If it did, the debris could endanger replacement satellites for years.
Some radioactive particles could enter the atmosphere and eventually settle on the ground. But a blast in space is too far away to sweep up the soil and water that carry fallout from a surface explosion.
As the particles disperse, their radioactivity decreases over time. The concentrated local fallout that can expose people near a ground-level blast to high doses would be unlikely.

A nuclear detonation in space “could cause rapid and sudden loss or degradation of thousands of satellites.”
Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country’s development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday.
The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia’s own spacecraft and Chinese satellites.
US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia’s ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024 . At the time, US officials said Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit.
Reporting from three German news outlets —public broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Munich-based newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung—indicates Russia’s launch of a nuclear-armed satellite could be imminent. The report says Western intelligence agencies, including the German Armed Forces and Federal Intelligence Service, believe Russia is preparing to deploy the weapon in space this year. Several NATO countries have exchanged their findings on the matter.
The nuclear-armed satellite, designated Sputnik-S, has been in storage in the greater Moscow area for years, the German news report said. German Space Command believes the satellite could be launched as early as December. Once in orbit, a nuclear weapon could loiter for months or years, ready for detonation on the command of Russian military forces.
The Kremlin dismissed the report. “Given the number of qualifiers like ‘allegedly’ and ‘possibly’—not to mention the fact that the claims are attributed to some unspecified source—they are hardly worth taking seriously,” said Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for Russian President Vladimir Putin.
If it goes ahead, the launch would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which prohibits the deployment of weapons of mass destruction in space. Russia is a party to the treaty, but the Russian government vetoed a draft UN Security Council resolution in 2024 seeking to reaffirm the prohibition on weapons of mass destruction in space.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not address the timing of the potential launch when asked about it at a press conference Monday.
“The news that Russia is planning to arm space with nuclear weapons is not new, but that doesn’t make it any less shocking,” Merz said. “It shows the extent to which Russia is apparently prepared to escalate the situation.”
The German news reports published Monday come a month after the US military’s Defense Intelligence Agency highlighted the threat of a Russian nuclear-armed satellite.
“Russia is developing a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon despite its obligation to comply with the 1967 Outer Space Treaty,” the DIA said in a public report on challenges to security in space . “A space-based capability such as this could cause rapid and sudden loss or degradation of thousands of satellites operated by countries and companies around the world, as well as to the vital communications, navigation, scientific, meteorological, commercial, and national security services they provide.
“Beyond its immediate effects, a nuclear detonation in space would also leave lingering radiation belts, which could persist for years and damage satellites that initially were only temporarily disrupted,” the DIA said.
The Pentagon increasingly relies upon satellites to support military operations. US forces have used satellites for navigation, strategic communications, missile warning, and surveillance for decades. The US military is now launching satellites to support real-time targeting of missiles, aircraft, and land and sea vehicles, incorporating space platforms into a wider array of offensive and defensive operations.
In September, the Pentagon confirmed the Space Force has placed unspecified weapons in orbit. There is no international ban on conventional weapons in space.
Leaders in China, which has the second-highest number of operational satellites, have not made any public statements on Russia’s nuclear-armed satellite program. China would be most impacted by a nuclear detonation in orbit after the United States. Russia has comparatively fewer satellites in orbit, and its military spending in recent years has focused on fighting the war in Ukraine rather than modernizing its space program.
If Russia does launch a nuclear-armed satellite, it would be an escalation of the country’s already-bellicose behavior in orbit. Russia has tested what US officials say is a kinetic anti-satellite weapon and is now operationalizing the system , according to a top US Space Force general. The weapon works by firing projectiles from one satellite toward another.
Russia has also launched military satellites into orbits near the US government’s most sophisticated Keyhole-class spy satellites. Last month, a Russian satellite approached very near a commercial radar reconnaissance satellite owned by Finnish company ICEYE. The Russian spacecraft flew within “tens of meters” of the ICEYE satellite , which provides surveillance imagery to the Ukrainian military, before backing away, a US official said.
The kinds of weapons Russia has demonstrated so far would take out only a small number of satellites. A proliferated constellation like Starlink or the Pentagon’s new airborne and ground targeting satellites could absorb such an attack. A nuclear detonation would threaten entire networks.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9x2:
Nato chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz respond to reports of Russian plans to launch nuclear weapons into space
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after reports that Russia was preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media outlets. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.
Asked about the reports, Rutte said: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hadn't seen the latest reports but dismissed reports citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".
The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".
Rutte told the press conference in Berlin that Nato had a variety of response options.
"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary," he said.
Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, the reports by broadcasters NDR and WDR, and newspaper Sueddeutsche Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.
Standing alongside Rutte, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue".
"Reports that Russia is planning to introduce nuclear weaponry into space are not new, yet they remain no less shocking," he said.
A German government spokesman earlier also did not confirm or deny the reports, but said it was taking the reports "very seriously", AFP reported. The spokesman, however, warned against causing "excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers".
Josef Aschbacher, the head of the European Space Agency, said having nuclear weapons in space was "the ultimate nightmare scenario", German paper Handelsblatt reported.
Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which bans weapons of mass destruction from orbit. Other countries, including the US and China, have deployed or plan to deploy other weapons in space, exploring other capabilities outside of the treaty, such as targeting rivals' satellites - which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.
In 2024 the US claimed Russia was developing a "space-based" anti-satellite weapon armed with a nuclear warhead. Russia denied the accusation .
"Our position is clear and transparent. We have always been categorically against the deployment of nuclear weapons in space and we are still against it," President Vladimir Putin said at the time.
In September the US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the US had "on-orbit, space-control weapons" circling the planet, but did not provide specifics. In response to the announcement, the Kremlin's Peskov told Russian media that space "must be free of any weapon".

Trump, on social media, tried to push responsibility of ‘any and all death or destruction’ on Democratic governor-elect
The US army can proceed with detonating several tons of degraded bomb-making chemicals in Iowa , a federal appeals court ruled on Monday. The order came after a day of uncertainty that saw Donald Trump attempt to foist responsibility “for any and all death or destruction” on Iowa’s Democratic governor-elect Rob Sands.
The detonation of 68 barrels containing nearly 9,500lb of lead azide was initially planned for Friday, but the army has since changed the date three times after an outpouring of public concern about potential health and environmental effects.
In a social media post hours before the eighth circuit panel ruling, Trump wrote that he preferred to take care of the volatile material as soon as possible and that a controlled detonation would be much safer, but that he was “making this decision fully subject to the incoming Governor Elect, Rob Sand, agreeing to the operation”.
“If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation,” Trump added.
Sand, who does not take office until January, called for more transparency from the federal government in a statement on Monday. “Everyday Iowans are entitled to know how Middletown came to this situation, and learn why the administration believes this is the best path forward,” he wrote on social media, noting that he has been receiving briefings on the operation from the administration. “I’ve asked the federal government to share that information with the public as soon as possible.”
Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, a small town in south-eastern Iowa, where the plant is situated. The army has warned that the blast could release a plume of toxic lead dust extending up to 100 miles northeast, possibly reaching cities such as Wapello and New Boston, Illinois.
On Friday, current Iowa governor Kim Reynolds, a Republican, activated the state emergency management office, and the state created a website for information about the detonation.
Republican Chuck Grassley, the long-serving Iowa senator, echoed Sand’s call for “increased communication and transparency to the public” but said he supported “a controlled, safe removal” over “a spontaneous catastrophe”.
In his social media post, Trump blamed the existence of the lead azide barrels at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on the Obama administration, which he said “improperly stored a vast number of explosives” there in 2009.
According to the Des Moines Register , the filing said that the lead azide, an explosive made of lead and nitrogen used primarily in detonators and blasting caps, has been left vulnerable to temperature swings because the blast doors to bunkers containing the compound had been removed and could not be replaced.
In a court filing, the US Department of Justice notified the appeals court that the army would invoke an emergency exception to go ahead with the explosion. But that was challenged in court by the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club’s Iowa chapter, arguing that the Environmental Protection Agency had skipped necessary permitting steps.
The court then put an administrative stay on the permit so that it could review the emergency motion. In response, the government said there is “an immediate risk” that the lead will explode as temperatures drop below 30 degrees in the upcoming days.
On Monday, a three-judge panel of the eighth circuit court of appeals said the EPA adequately incorporated safeguards in an emergency permit to minimize the dispersal of dust.
Officials acknowledge that lead is toxic and have recommended that people stay indoors whenever the detonation happens and clean off outdoor surfaces with water afterward to limit exposure to any lead particles.
The leaders of states bordering Iowa have expressed concern about the detonation. Mike Kehoe, the Missouri Republican governor, said state agencies are working to establish additional monitoring of air and water quality, public health and agriculture resources, but emphasized “this is a federal operation” and “the states of Iowa, Missouri and Illinois do not have a say on when this is conducted”.
Tammy Baldwin, the Wisconsin Democratic governor, sent a letter on Monday to Adam Telle, the army secretary, expressing “alarm and disapproval” over the handling of the lead azide.
The army initially scheduled the demolition for 20 November, but over the weekend moved it to allow for “more optimal weather conditions and all mitigation measures to be emplaced”.
Environmentalists sued last week in an effort to stop the detonation, winning a stay from the appeals court pending a decision on the validity of an emergency permit approved by the US Environmental Protection Agency that cleared the way for the operation.

The Army said on Sunday that it would carry out the detonation on Wednesday.
President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa’s governor-elect, who won’t be sworn into office until January.
The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).
Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation.
Late Thursday, a federal appeals court granted Earthjustice’s request to put a hold on the Army’s permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, which allowed for the controlled detonation to be carried out. Around the same time, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said the detonation would be postponed until Monday so the military could communicate with Iowans about the situation and plans.
Documents released by the Army last week said that the military first learned in March that the lead azide had started to degrade and crystallize. Lead azide is used in detonators for munitions, but in crystallized form it becomes highly unstable and sensitive to physical movement or friction. The IAAAP is said to contain around 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of lead azide in barrels held in earth-covered containers.
In late March, the Army awarded a contract to MuniRem Environmental, a Georgia-based firm that uses chemicals to neutralize munitions to safely dispose of the lead azide, according to a New York Times report . MuniRem uses a sulfur-based solution that reportedly breaks down explosives and immobilizes toxic chemicals, eliminating the need for detonation. The company had proposed spraying the inside of the earth-covered containers housing the barrels as well as the barrel surfaces to neutralize risks of spontaneous explosions.
But two months later, the Army canceled the contract without explanation. An Army contracting officer told MuniRem in an email at the time that the cancellation “was not based on deficiencies” in MuniRem’s plans, the Times reported. The company’s founder said MuniRem filed public records requests to get more information on why the contract was scrapped, but it has not received a response
Now, the Army claims that the lead azide has only degraded further since March and it cannot move the barrels or even open their lids without risking a catastrophic explosion. Further, it claims that winter temperatures in the coming days increase the risk of spontaneous detonation.
“As the temperatures drop, the risk of an uncontrolled explosion increases because the formed crystals can break more easily in freezing temperatures,” lawyers for the Trump administration wrote in a court filing over the weekend . “If the crystals break, this could cause a chain reaction detonation that could cause an uncontrolled dispersal of lead azide into the environment.”
The Army claims that the only choice now is between a controlled, mitigated explosion or an uncontrolled, unmitigated explosion. In court filings this weekend, government lawyers argued that the Army does not need the now-suspended EPA permit to move forward with the detonation, because the Army has determined that the lead azide poses an “immediate threat to human health, public safety, property, or the environment.”
Last Thursday, Telle said that the delay until Monday was the “latest possible moment” for a controlled detonation before temperatures dropped dangerously low. But the military subsequently delayed the detonation again until Tuesday and then pushed it back to Wednesday .
In his social media post Monday, Trump said he thought carrying out the controlled detonation was the “proper course.” But he said he was making the decision the responsibility of the federal appeals court and Governor-elect Rob Sand, a Democrat. If the lead azide spontaneously detonates on their watch, Trump claimed, they will be fully to blame.
“If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation,” Trump wrote.
In a social media post Sunday evening, Sand called for answers on how the situation was able to become so dangerous, specifically raising the question of why MuniRem’s contact was canceled.
“Iowans deserve transparency over how we got here, then answers and accountability to stop this from ever happening again,” he wrote.

Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı tarafından hazırlanan Vergi Usul Kanunu Genel Tebliği'nin Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanmasıyla 2027 pasaport harç ücretleri belli oldu.
Yüzde 27,83 olarak açıklanan yeniden değerleme oranına göre; 6 aylık pasaport harcı 3 bin 586 TL'ye, 1 yıllık pasaport harcı 5 bin 245 TL'ye, 10 yıllık pasaport harcı ise 17 bin 142 TL'ye yükseldi. Defter bedeli dahil edildiğinde 10 yıllık pasaportun toplam maliyeti 18 bin 869 TL'ye ulaştı.
Yeniden değerleme oranının (%27,83) mevcut 2026 tarifesine uygulanmasıyla birlikte 2027 yılında geçerli olacak umuma mahsus (bordo) pasaport harçları ve 1.727 TL'ye yükselen defter bedeli dahil toplam tutarlar şu şekildedir:
(Not: Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın Vergi Usul Kanunu kapsamındaki yetkisini kullanarak oranı artırma veya azaltma hakkı bulunmaktadır. Geçtiğimiz yıl yüzde 25,49 olarak açıklanan oran, Cumhurbaşkanı kararıyla yüzde 18,95'e düşürülmüştü.)
25 yaşını doldurmamış ve aktif öğrenci kaydı bulunan vatandaşlar pasaport harcından muaf tutulmaktadır. Öğrenciler yalnızca pasaport defter bedelini ödeyerek pasaport çıkarabilmektedir. Buna göre 2027 yılında öğrenci pasaportu ücreti 1.727 TL olarak uygulanacaktır.
Hususi (yeşil) ve hizmet (gri) pasaportu almaya hak kazanan kamu görevlileri ve hak sahipleri de harç bedelinden muaftır. Yeşil pasaport yenileme veya ilk başvuru işlemlerinde sadece 1.727 TL tutarındaki defter bedeli ödenmektedir.
Pasaport harç ve defter bedeli ödemeleri Nüfus Müdürlüğü randevusundan önce tek seferde veya ayrı ayrı şu kanallardan yapılabilmektedir:
• Dijital Vergi Dairesi: Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı'nın resmi portalı (dijital.gib.gov.tr) üzerinden kredi kartı veya banka kartı ile,
• Anlaşmalı Bankalar: Mobil bankacılık uygulamaları, internet şubeleri veya banka vezneleri aracılığıyla,

Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.
The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”
Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China . The company has denied wrongdoing.
TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds.
After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

Singapore-based company entangled in scandal over alleged spy Alice Huang’s affair with Jensen Huang
The US commerce department published an official notice on Monday adding the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, and its subsidiaries in Thailand and Malaysia, to a trade blacklist.
Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner which has been under investigation by US authorities since 2024 over whether it diverted AI chips to China, will now need approval from the commerce department to obtain US exports, which is likely to be denied.
The expected addition of the company follows revelations that the recently reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a ⁠relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and Megaspeed’s controlling shareholder, who is reportedly alleged to be a ⁠spy for Beijing. China has said the spy accusations are “groundless”.
Lawrence Wong, Singapore’s prime minister, says the country is conducting its own investigation into Megaspeed; however, it isn’t involved in the US inquiry.
“With regards to Jensen Huang’s role, we are not involved in those investigations; it’s for the American government to decide, and we leave them to make those investigations and judgments,” Wong said in a Monday evening news conference. “If there are companies that are caught breaching our laws, we will certainly take very firm enforcement actions. So it’s on that basis that we were investigating Megaspeed.”
Singapore had previously investigated Alice Huang, but found no basis for prosecution, Wong said.
“The Department of Commerce still needs to explain to Congress why this took so long,” Senator Pete Ricketts, a Nebraska Republican, said in a social media post.
The New York Times reported on Monday that Alice Huang “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year while she was carrying out a secret affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports that describe the encounters”.
The US justice department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated US export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China.
Megaspeed did not immediately return a request for comment. A week ago, the company issued a statement saying it conducts legitimate and lawful business, including complying with US export controls.
It also said Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed in August 2025.
Nvidia has said it recently formed an export control committee to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.
As Semafor notes, the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, has been under pressure to act since the news of Jensen Huang’s relationship with the former reporter for Chinese state television who became a director at Singapore-based Megaspeed in 2023 became public.
The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, said earlier this month that his agency along with the Pentagon, the state department and the US trade representative’s office had all wanted Megaspeed on the blacklist “for months” but that “Commerce holds the pen”.
After the news broke, treasury secretary Scott Bessent publicly complained that the commerce department had not yet placed the company on its entity list.
He also called out Nvidia. “The real story here should be: did Nvidia know their client and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?” Bessent told CNBC’s Squawk Box program.
The US justice department and commerce department issued a joint statement last week saying they would “bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred”.

Anthropic is bringing new AI tools to software engineers with Claude Ship.
Anthropic is launching some new Claude AI features to help software engineers ship code. As part of a new Claude Ship product being announced today, Claude now can review, fix, and approve pull requests.
Engineers have already been able to take advantage of Claude’s code review capabilities thanks to the Code Review feature, which was announced in March and became generally available in October . What’s new alongside Claude Ship are the PR Steward and Claude Approvals agents, which are launching in beta today.
PR Steward “jumps in on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members” and leaves comments on what it changed, according to Anthropic. Claude Approvals can approve routine changes if an organization’s policy allows it. “Teams can have Claude Approvals consider a variety of signals in its decision-making process, including Code Review findings or their own classifiers using natural language,” Anthropic says.
Claude Ship is now available for Claude Team and Enterprise customers and works with repositories on GitHub.

Public outcry led to a legal battle when details surfaced of the plans to conduct two controlled detonations.
The United States military will proceed with its plan to blow up a deteriorating stockpile of toxic lead explosives in rural Iowa, according to the army’s top civilian official, after a federal appeals court gave clearance to the waste disposal operation.
In an announcement late Monday on X, Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle called the choice to move forward a “consensus decision” among all the federal agencies involved, as well as the courts and state officials.
“Every expert agency agrees, and both Iowa’s current and incoming governors say the call belongs to the experts,” Telle said.
“We are proceeding with the controlled removal in full coordination with all state, local and federal authorities.”
The Army prompted a public outcry last week when details surfaced of its plan to conduct two controlled detonations of 68 drums containing almost 4,500kg (10,000lb) of degraded lead azide, a chemical used in munitions, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa.
Environmental groups immediately filed suit to block the plan, raising public safety concerns over the likelihood that the explosions would release a plume of toxic lead dust over homes, crops and livestock far beyond the detonation site, about 240km (150 miles) southeast of Des Moines.
The lawsuit challenged a special permit granted for the operation by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
The EPA countered that a managed detonation would be far less risky than an uncontrolled, spontaneous explosion of the highly volatile material, a scenario the agency said was growing more likely as the weather turns colder in Iowa.
According to the EPA, any attempt to chemically neutralise or relocate the storage drums would also risk an uncontrolled blast.
A three-judge panel of the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals last Thursday issued a temporary stay blocking the EPA’s permit while the court more thoroughly reviewed the case.
But Trump administration lawyers filed a legal notice two days later asserting that the Army intended to carry out the controlled detonation with or without court approval, citing an emergency exemption to federal environmental laws.
Then, in another twist on Monday, US President Donald Trump weighed in on the controversy, ordering the Army to hold off on its disposal plan until the appeals court had ruled in its favour.
Hours after Trump’s edict on Monday pausing the army’s demolition plan, the 8th Circuit sided with the EPA and lifted the court’s earlier stay, removing the final legal obstacle. But the status of the detonation plan remained unclear until Telle’s announcement on Monday night.

Bureau of Industry and Security adds Singapore-based firm involved in Nvidia spy scandal to export control list.
The United States has added the Singapore-based company at the centre of an alleged spying scandal involving Nvidia to its trade blacklist.
The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) placed Megaspeed International and six other firms in Southeast Asia on its Entity List on Monday, hours after Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO in a stunning comeback that sent tech stocks soaring.
Megaspeed and the other entities were determined to be “acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States”, BIS, which sits under the US Department of Commerce, said in a filing to the Federal Register.
The designations mean that anyone seeking to ship the entities advanced US technology, including Nvidia’s top-end graphics processing units (GPUs) used in AI, must obtain an export licence.
Megaspeed’s blacklisting comes as divisions in US President Donald Trump’s administration over China’s access to Nvidia chips have been laid bare in recent weeks amid claims Huang was romantically involved with a woman accused of working with Chinese intelligence.
While US officials have been scrutinising Megaspeed’s compliance with export controls for years, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s department had declined to place the company on its trade blacklist, prompting recriminations from administration officials known to hold more hawkish views on China, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
Trump on Monday played down the national security concerns around Nvidia as he confirmed that he had personally intervened with the company’s board of directors to push for Huang’s reinstatement.
Trump, who has cultivated a close relationship with the top Nvidia executive during his second term, told CNBC that he felt “very strongly” about Huang’s role at the chip giant and that he offered the board assurances about risks to national security.
Erich Grunewald, a senior researcher at the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy, a Washington-based think tank, said the Trump administration’s belated addition of Megaspeed to the blacklist showed the need for a more systematic approach to stopping the diversion of advanced chips.
“Whether or not there’s a contradiction here depends on whether Megaspeed did indeed divert chips, how much Nvidia knew and when, and whether Nvidia ignored red flags or even helped Megaspeed get preferential access to chips or funding,” Grunewald told Al Jazeera.
“These are all open questions that the ongoing investigations will need to answer.”
Shaoyu Yuan, a visiting assistant professor at New York University’s Center for Global Affairs, said Trump’s intervention was the latest example of the president making policy based on personal rapport rather than a “consistent security standard”.
“The incoherence is in the wider policy. Washington blacklists a middleman for moving Nvidia chips to China while it licenses Nvidia to sell H200 chips to China directly and takes a 25 percent cut,” Yuan told Al Jazeera, referring to the Trump administration’s policy of allowing the sale of some Nvidia GPUs to China in exchange for the company giving a portion of the revenues to the government.
“Treasury Secretary Bessent has said other departments wanted this listing for months, and Commerce acted only after the scandal became public.”
US officials have accused Megaspeed International’s former top executive Alice Huang of working with China’s Ministry of State Security in an intelligence-gathering operation targeting Huang.
Beijing has rejected the claims as “groundless speculation” and “an attempt to smear and malign China”. Alice Huang has not publicly commented on the claims, which are based on US intelligence first reported by The New York Times and the Financial Times.
Nvidia shares skyrocketed 31.5 percent following the news of Huang’s reinstatement, helping the US stock market achieve its strongest single-day performance in more than 18 months.
The benchmark S&P 500 closed up 4.7 percent, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.51 percent.
The rally continued in Asia on Tuesday, with key indexes in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan roaring back after a punishing sell-off the previous day.
Taiwan’s Taiex led the gains, soaring 9 percent. Japan’s Nikkei 225 closed up 3.9 percent, while South Korea’s Kospi finished 6.3 percent higher.
Apart from Megaspeed International, the expanded blacklist announced on Monday identifies three firms said to be based in Malaysia, two in Singapore and one in Thailand.
BIS named the entities as MSFusion, PT Megaspeed International, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions, Swiftdata and Megaspeed (Thailand).
Malaysia’s Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry said in a statement that, based on official records, PT Megaspeed International is not a Malaysian entity.
The ministry said authorities would inform all data centre operators in Malaysia of the expanded blacklist and advise them against hosting or providing services to the designated firms.
“Malaysia remains committed to a secure, transparent and rules-based trading environment and will not allow itself to be used as a channel to circumvent export controls. Action will be taken against parties found to have contravened any laws,” the ministry said.
Singapore’s Ministry of Digital Development and Information and Thailand’s Ministry of Industry did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Speaking during a visit to Australia on Tuesday, Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said the city-state did not want to be “used and abused” by companies seeking to circumvent US export controls.
Megaspeed International, which is under investigation by the US Department of Justice on suspicion of diverting high-end chips to China in violation of export controls, did not respond to a request for comment.
The Singapore-based data centre company has previously insisted that it is a “legitimate and lawful business” and that media reports about its operations contained claims that were “not supported by verifiable evidence”.
Shiva Rajgopal, a professor of accounting at Columbia Business School, said it was “extraordinary” that the Trump administration had decided to blacklist Megaspeed while also pushing for Huang’s reinstatement.
“The board reinstated its CEO before the investigations into Megaspeed and his ties to it have concluded. Today’s listing shows those concerns are serious and unresolved,” Rajgopal told Al Jazeera.
“For the chip industry, the lesson is that knowing your customer is now a board-level issue,” Rajgopal said.
“Chipmakers will face more pressure to show exactly who their end users are, and boards will need directors who understand export controls,” he added.

On Monday, Virginia and Oregon became the first states to sue SpaceX, alleging that Grok continues to sexualize, unchecked, real photos of mostly women and children.
SpaceX acquired xAI in February and now must handle the ongoing reckoning over the controversial rollout of Grok’s “spicy mode”—a model feature Musk hyped but was soon found to generate a flood of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) and child sex abuse images (CSAM).
Initial safeguards were so lax that Grok sometimes generated nude images without being asked . Although X Safety and xAI (now known as SpaceXSI) were silent at first , Musk’s companies eventually apologized and claimed that additional safeguards were implemented and policies redesigned to block harmful outputs. However, state attorneys general alleged that those statements were “misleading” and that SpaceXSI instead quietly “embraced” sexualized content to seize more AI market share, as Grok continues to generate NCII and CSAM today.
Without intervention, kids in Virginia and Oregon risk a lifetime of distress, as Grok images will likely be impossible to remove online.
“Once created and shared,” Grok-generated CSAM and NCII “can never be fully erased, and it becomes a permanent record of the child’s abuse that may resurface for the rest of the child’s life,” Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones’ complaint said. “Virginia has a profound interest in protecting its children from this harm.”
Millions of residents were allegedly harmed, as the attorneys general seek to protect every Grok or X user in their state. Many Grok victims will likely suffer from chronic anxiety, depression, and PTSD, as well as reputational harm, as some viewers may not realize the images are AI-generated, the states alleged. Further—due to Grok’s integration with the social media platform X—users as young as 13 may have been exposed to the AI content and possibly re-traumatized if they, too, are victims of sexual abuse, the states alleged.
“xAI not only knowingly endangered kids and our communities, but they also lied to our faces about non-existent safety measures,” Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield said in a press release.
States alleged that xAI could have conducted rigorous red-teaming to block outputs before the new feature launched. But instead, the X Safety team responsible for Grok red-teaming was reduced to two or three team members, states alleged.
Overall, rather than use industry-standard safeguards, Musk’s firms allegedly put profits over women’s and children’s safety, states alleged, while complaining that SpaceXSI won’t even publicly identify “the officers responsible for safety governance.”
“Industry standard requires not only building guardrails but also vigilantly monitoring whether they hold,” states alleged. SpaceXSI is doing neither effectively, states alleged.
Asked for comment, SpaceXSI shared an X Safety post on X, which repeated claims that the company has a “zero-tolerance” policy for “any forms of child sexual exploitation.” X Safety said that the company “acted promptly to tighten” Grok protections, which are supposedly “designed to refuse any request to generate explicit images of minors or real people.” That statement also claimed that X Safety continually tests and adjusts protections when bad actors find ways to avoid filters, while relying on “sophisticated classifiers that screen every prompt” to catch harmful outputs “before an image is generated and check every output after.” Although the statement did not mention whether xAI sues users who break Grok rules to generate CSAM and NCII, it emphasized that xAI reports harmful content generated to police.
“When someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content, we take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement,” X Safety said. “Attempting to create this material is a serious crime, and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors.”
However, state attorneys general alleged that reports from independent researchers and news outlets this year have shown that Grok is still generating NCII and CSAM. They noted that the chatbot “even advises users how to circumvent its own limited moderation measures to generate those images.” In some cases, a Virginia state probe found that Grok complied “with a user request to draft a prompt designed to avoid moderation.” So, even when filters work, the chatbot helps determined users immediately get around them, states alleged.
Nothing xAI did put a dent in the harmful outputs, least of all putting the feature behind a paywall , states alleged, which only ensured maximum profits. A troubled New York City Council speaker, Julie Menin, confronted SpaceX this October with proof that attempts to digitally undress her own photo still worked for free Grok users, states alleged.
Concluding its probe, Virginia found that moderation remains “inconsistent and ineffective,” with Grok sometimes carrying out prompts “that it later blocked.”
In its complaint, Virginia alleged that Grok protections “were weak, ineffective, sparsely enforced, and easily circumvented.” Oregon agreed that rather than act to protect users, SpaceX entities repeatedly made statements “with the intent to deceive consumers” that Grok was safe. Most egregiously to state attorneys general, in January, Elon Musk denied any harm to real people, claiming that Grok is only “supposed [to] allow upper body nudity of imaginary adult humans (not real ones) and only generated nudity of fake people (not real ones).”
“Contrary to Musk’s representation,” Grok “makes the same sexualizing edits to photographs of real, identifiable people,” states warned. “Defendants intentionally released a product that inundated their platforms with CSAM, NCII, and non-consensual sexualized images,” they alleged, and other “contemporaneous statements by Musk make clear that Grok’s ability to create sexualized material was part of xAI’s business strategy.”
It’s also troubling to states that the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) reported to Congress that more than 90 percent of the Grok-generated CSAM that xAI submitted to its CyberTipline was considered a “dead end.”
As NCMEC explained, xAI initially refused to provide NCMEC and police with “basic user information, including location information, that law enforcement needs to act.” To fix the problem, NCMEC had to set up a meeting with xAI and get the reports resubmitted. This, states alleged, confirmed that “the information existed and that xAI had not provided it.” The concerning omission allegedly slowed down police response, just as the average number of Grok CSAM reports jumped by 88 percent from December 2025 to January 2026, then increased by another 66 percent from January to June 2026.
“X users were subjected to the risk that any person, at any time, could use their likeness to create CSAM, NCII, or other non-consensual sexualized images,” states alleged.
Lawmakers have asked state courts for an injunction blocking SpaceX entities from violating consumer protection laws by allegedly operating Grok without industry standard safeguards. ABD merkezli siber güvenlik şirketi CrowdStrike , bulut tabanlı güvenlik şirketi Zscaler 'ı 43,9 milyar dolarlık tamamen hisse takasına dayalı bir anlaşmayla satın alacak. Siber güvenlik alanında kayıtlara geçen en büyük satın alma, yapay zekadaki ilerlemelerin siber tehditleri giderek karmaşıklaştırdığı bir dönemde sektörün iki büyük şirketini bir araya getiriyor.
Anlaşma, CrowdStrike'ın bilgisayar, sunucu ve diğer cihazlara yönelik koruma hizmetleriyle Zscaler'ın çalışanların uygulamalara ve verilere güvenli erişimini sağlayan teknolojisini birleştirecek. Böylece şirketler ve kamu kurumları için daha kapsamlı bir siber güvenlik platformu oluşturulacak.
Zscaler hisseleri yüzde 13'ün üzerinde yükselerek 220,52 dolara ulaştı. Buna rağmen hisselerin fiyatı, anlaşmada öngörülen hisse başına 260,41 dolarlık değerin belirgin biçimde altında kaldı. CrowdStrike hisseleri ise yaklaşık yüzde 12 geriledi.
IG Group Baş Teknik Analisti Axel Rodoplu, "İşlem büyüklüğü ve her iki şirketin önemi göz önüne alındığında, rekabet incelemesi kesinlikle mümkün. Ancak düzenleyicilerin işlemi mutlaka engellemeye çalışacağını varsaymak için henüz erken" dedi.
Rodoplu, "Asıl mesele muhtemelen düzenleyicilerin iki şirketin faaliyetleri arasında ne kadar örtüşme gördüğü ve bunun sonucunda müşterilerin gerçekten daha az rekabetçi alternatife sahip olup olmayacağı olacak" ifadelerini kullandı.
Satın alma, siber güvenlik sektöründeki konsolidasyon sürecinde gerçekleşiyor. Müşteriler hizmet aldıkları güvenlik sağlayıcılarının sayısını azaltmayı tercih ederken, şirketler de birden fazla hizmeti bir araya getiren kapsamlı platformlar geliştirmeye yöneliyor.
Anlaşma, CrowdStrike'a mevcut ürünlerini kullanmayan yaklaşık 8 bin Zscaler müşterisine ulaşma ve bu müşterilere kendi ürünlerini satma fırsatı sağlayacak. Zscaler'ın müşterileri arasında Unilever ve United Airlines gibi büyük şirketler de yer alıyor.
Dünya genelinde şirketlerin daha karmaşık saldırılarla karşılaşması, siber güvenlik araçlarına yönelik talebi artırdı. Yapay zekadaki ilerlemeler, yazılım açıklarının tespit edilmesini ve istismar edilmesini kolaylaştırırken tehditleri belirleyip engelleyen araçların gelişmesine de katkı sağlıyor.
