Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.
The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.
“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.
The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available , and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.
Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.
Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.
Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.
Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

Users can give agents tasks such as booking travel or buying presents, but glitches have been reported
Want to avoid the Christmas shopping hordes? Then let your AI agent do it. Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta is launching its Muse AI assistant in the UK and is encouraging users to let it loose on their apps – and the high street.
Muse has been a hit in the US and is ranked first and second respectively on Google and Apple’s free app store, having been downloaded millions of times.
Muse can be used as an app or directly within Meta’s WhatsApp messaging platform. Meta invites users to give their assistant a name, a look and a personality, so they can talk to it as well as assign it tasks such as sending an email, booking travel or buying festive presents.
“From doing the Christmas shopping and searching for a cheaper energy deal, to sorting the school calendar … Muse can get it done for you,” said Meta.
Meta acknowledged that handing control of your day-to-day digital life to an AI agent is “an act of trust”. Muse cannot make a purchase or send an email without your permission and will only connect to apps you let it join. The app has no visibility into people’s passwords or payment methods, Meta said, and it does not share your conversations with advertisers. It will ask for your approval before making a purchase or sending an email, while a separate “security agent” checks Muse’s actions against the permissions you’ve granted.
“Think of it as a helping hand for the jobs that pile up, like chasing a refund, renewing car insurance or keeping on top of the school calendar,” said Meta. “To get those jobs done, you can connect Muse to the apps you already use, from your email and calendar to the retailer apps you shop on.”
Meta said it has signed deals with an array of British businesses – including Marks & Spencer, electrical retailer Currys, Sainsbury’s and easyJet – allowing Muse to navigate their websites more easily.
In a statement last month UK regulators including the Competition and Markets Authority and the Information Commissioner’s Office said AI agents – the term for AI programmes that carry out series of tasks without human intervention – could “unlock wider innovation” but could also “amplify and accelerate risks and introduce new ones”. The watchdogs said concerns such as fraud, scams and misuse of personal information needed to be addressed by companies providing personal AI agents .
Reuters reported last week that Meta employees had raised concerns about the app’s performance, including one staff member receiving a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an encrypted messaging app. In another example reported by Reuters, Muse delivered a message with random bank account balances in it.
Meta said internal testing is vital for product development and allows the company to implement safety and privacy protection before releasing anything publicly. It is understood the majority of problems flagged by Reuters related to a bug that has been fixed.
Muse is powered by Muse Spark, Meta’s first model from the company’s “super intelligence” AI lab . In a social media post on Sunday, Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, raised the possibility of humanity losing control over AI systems that are able to improve themselves autonomously.
“It is … hard to imagine a world where humanity maintains control with super intelligence that is 1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field,” he wrote.
Responding to reports that AI had cracked one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics – the Riemann hypothesis – Wang said the tech industry needed to make progress in the “extremely urgent” areas of AI safety, security and alignment. Alignment refers to ensuring an AI system adheres to human goals and values.

Herhangi bir indirim düzenlemesi yapılmaması halinde 1 Ocak 2027 itibarıyla geçerli olacak yeni tarifeye göre; otomobil, minibüs ve kamyonet muayene ücreti 3 bin 288 TL'den 4 bin 203 TL'ye yükseldi. Evlilik nedeniyle soyadı değişikliği yapacak vatandaşlar, kimlik kartı yenileme tarifesine tabidir. Buna göre 2027 yılında evlilik sonrası kimlik yenileme işlemi için 281,20 TL değerli kağıt bedeli ödenecektir. (Not: Evlilik cüzdanı bedeli ayrı olarak tahsil edilmektedir.)
Kimlik kartı değerli kağıt bedeli ödemeleri Nüfus Müdürlüğü randevusundan önce şu kanallardan yapılabilmektedir:
• Dijital Vergi Dairesi: Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı'nın resmi portalı (dijital.gib.gov.tr) üzerinden kredi kartı veya banka kartı ile,
• Anlaşmalı Bankalar: Ziraat Bankası, VakıfBank, Halkbank ve diğer anlaşmalı bankaların mobil uygulamaları veya internet şubeleri aracılığıyla,
• PTT ve Vergi Daireleri: PTT şubeleri ile vergi dairesi veznelerinden nakit olarak. Ödeme yapıldıktan sonra Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri Genel Müdürlüğü'nün ALO 199 hattından veya randevu.nvi.gov.tr adresinden randevu alınması gerekmektedir.
Kayıp kimlik ücreti neden iki katı olarak ödeniyor?
Nüfus Hizmetleri Kanunu gereğince kimlik kartının kaybedilmesi veya çalınması durumunda, standart yenileme (değiştirme) bedelinin iki katı tutarında değerli kağıt bedeli tahsil edilmektedir. Eski nüfus cüzdanını yeni kimlikle değiştirmek zorunlu mu?
Eski tip nüfus cüzdanları resmi kurumlarda ve bankacılık işlemlerinde kimlik doğrulama güvenliği nedeniyle geçerliliğini yitirmeye başladığından en kısa sürede çipli T.C. More than a million people were forced to flee the violence across the border to Bangladesh in 2017
The UK has sanctioned five senior Myanmar military leaders after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that the country had carried out genocide against the Rohingya minority – marking the first time a state has been found guilty of the crime .
A military crackdown in 2017 killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar, formerly known as Burma.
The UK is joined by several other countries , external in acknowledging the ICJ ruling, including Australia, Belgium, Portugal, Spain and Canada.
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said: "Our response to a crime as profoundly shocking as genocide must reflect our values and must be matched by clear action."
Bowen: Myanmar genocide verdict is historic and could have far-reaching implications
The senior military leaders facing sanctions are Myo Htut Hlaing, Myo Min Tun, Myat Thet Oo, Kyaw Soe and Kyaw Swar Oo.
Miliband added that Myanmar's President Min Aung Hlaing , who was sanctioned by the UK in 2021, is "directly responsible for many of the atrocities that have happened" as he was head of the military at the time of the genocide in 2017.
He said: "Myanmar must stop ongoing violations, investigate, prosecute and punish perpetrators, and prevent such an atrocity from ever happening again."
Miliband also called for an "immediate pause in hostilities to enable humanitarian aid to get through, a stop to air strikes on civilians, and the release of political prisoners, as well as dialogue towards an inclusive political settlement".
The foreign secretary confirmed that new legislation would be passed to stop the supply of aviation fuel to the country, which was known as Burma until 1989.
Last week, he expelled Myanmar's defence attaché after the ICJ ruled the country had committed genocide during the brutal military campaign in 2017.
He told MPs on Monday the UK would raise the issue at the UN Security Council this week, and there would be a dedicated meeting in a fortnight.
The court found on Thursday that "genocidal intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence" it had seen.
The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world. The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention , external .
In its ruling last week, the court determined that about 10,000 Rohingya were murdered during the clearance operation in the western Rakhine state that borders Bangladesh and the Bay of Bengal. Myanmar denied the claims against it.
Reports said that entire villages were burnt down, and that women and girls were raped.
Miliband said more than 1.2 million refugees fled and were being supported by Bangladesh.
Myanmar's leader during the genocide, Aung San Suu Kyi , was deposed by the military in 2021.
MPs heard that air strikes and violence from the Arakan army were still happening.
'My family died in front of my eyes’: Harrowing tales from a Myanmar massacre

The Pakistan Air Force pilot will spend about a week on board the Tiangong, conducting experiments with China’s crew.
Islamabad, Pakistan – Pakistan is poised to send an astronaut into space for the first time on Wednesday, when an air force pilot joins China’s Shenzhou-24 mission to the country’s Tiangong space station.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, will fly as a payload specialist alongside commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. The spacecraft is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China at 8:18am Beijing time (00:18 GMT), or 5:18am in Pakistan.
Speaking at a news conference in Jiuquan on Tuesday, China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said the mission would mark the first joint flight by Chinese and foreign astronauts in the country’s crewed space programme.
After reaching orbit, the spacecraft will carry out a rapid, autonomous rendezvous lasting about three and a half hours before docking with the forward port of the station’s Tianhe core module, Zhang said.
Ali’s stay will be brief. He will return to Earth on board the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft after a short joint flight, while Zhu Yangzhu, a member of that crew, remains in orbit for a year, Zhang said.
Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) has said Ali will spend about a week on the station.
“I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis,” Ali told reporters during the crew’s conversation with the media.
Ali and Khurram Daud, a second Pakistani selected for astronaut training, are Pakistan Air Force pilots.
They were selected through a three-stage process that began with screening in Pakistan and included medical, psychological and technical assessments.
CMSA named them reserve astronauts on April 22 earlier this year. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met them in Islamabad the following day, and on April 24, China’s Space Day, they joined the Astronaut Center of China in Beijing for training.
Before leaving, Daud asked Pakistanis to pray for him in a video released by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
“My message to you all is to pray for me, so that I can complete this training and this mission well, and make my nation and my country proud,” he said in Urdu.
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who is in China for the launch, paid tribute to both men on X on Tuesday.
“They trained in centrifuges and simulators, in emergency drills and in a new language. Both performed exceptionally well in training. Though Zeeshan Ali will fly tomorrow both have already made Pakistan proud,” he wrote.
Thanking his instructors, SUPARCO and CMSA, at Tuesday’s news conference, Ali said: “No matter who flies, we have already made the history together.”
Daud was not named in the crew, and it is not yet clear whether he will fly on a later mission.
In written responses to Al Jazeera, SUPARCO said the backup astronauts would serve as experts to help carry the programme forward.
Zhang said Ali would take part in the crew’s daily work but would mainly oversee China-Pakistan experiments, install samples and equipment and conduct tests in orbit.
The mission will include four joint science projects in biotechnology and materials, Zhang said. Ali will also conduct an experiment involving cyanobacteria, photosynthetic microorganisms.
Pakistan’s Information Ministry said in April that the experiments would cover materials science, fluid physics, life sciences and biotechnology, with potential applications in climate resilience, food security and industrial innovation.
Qamarul Islam, a space scientist and former senior official in the state-affiliated Institute of Space Technology (IST) in Islamabad, said the experiments had been shortlisted after SUPARCO invited research institutes in Pakistan to submit proposals.
“Primarily these experiments are the experiments of the research institutes, universities and others, from Pakistan,” he told Al Jazeera.
SUPARCO said the station was a fully equipped laboratory. It added in its response that Ali’s week in orbit was meant to start and install the experiments, and to record data confirming that the equipment had survived launch loads and vibrations and was safely installed in microgravity.
“Completing the four experiments takes between six and 12 months,” it said.
According to Zhang, preparations focused on professional skills, crew coordination and language.
“We focus on Chinese commands and technical terms to ensure accurate execution,” he said, in the English interpretation of his remarks.
In a promotional video by the Chinese space agency, Ali, who described himself as a fighter pilot, said centrifuge, rescue and survival, and emergency procedures training were part of his preparation.
“But the real challenge, honestly speaking, was mastering the Chinese language, because all the switches, all the software, all the programmes, all the voice announcements, everything is in Chinese. So we had to learn that and master that technical Chinese,” he said.
SUPARCO and CMSA signed their astronaut agreement in Islamabad in February 2025. Ali said the two countries had since moved quickly.
“The two great nations of China and Pakistan have turned a pilot into an astronaut in a remarkably short span of time,” he said.
This year marks 75 years of diplomatic ties between the two neighbours. Zhang described the flight as another milestone in their cooperation.
“Pakistan is China’s all-weather strategic cooperative partner,” Zhang said, according to the English interpretation of his remarks.
Pakistan’s Information Ministry said in April that the programme placed the country among a select group of nations involved in human spaceflight.
China built its own space station after being excluded from the International Space Station (ISS), in part because a 2011 US law bars NASA from bilateral cooperation with Beijing.
“Chinese were left out. And obviously China developed their own space station. Pakistan is also out of the International Space Station as far as the astronauts are concerned,” Qamar said.
He said China’s decision to choose Pakistan for its first foreign visitor reflected the two countries’ closeness.
Asked by a reporter on Tuesday whether China would expand cooperation, including joint flights with Russia, Zhang pointed to the station’s transport and astronaut-training systems. He said China hoped to explore space with more countries and regions.
SUPARCO said Pakistan was opening a path for international collaboration on the Chinese station and could now offer its expertise to other countries.
Asked by China’s state-run CGTN about the future of the partnership, Ali looked beyond the current mission.
“I believe what comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself. This mission is not a finish line; it is a launchpad. And I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation to grow from one astronaut, one flight, to multiple joint flights, to Moon, Mars, and beyond.”
Asked about lunar plans, SUPARCO said Pakistan was already working with China on a lunar mission tentatively planned for 2028. It said it could not yet disclose details.
Pakistan’s lunar programme has so far focused on robotic missions. The iCube-Qamar satellite, developed at IST, reached the lunar orbit on board China’s Chang’e-6 mission in 2024. A SUPARCO-developed rover is due to fly on the Chang’e-8 about 2028.
Qamar, who was the project director for iCube-Qamar, said lunar missions ranged from flybys and orbiters, such as the satellite, to landings and eventually permanent bases.
“In the long term you will see stations on the Moon, a utilisation of the Moon,” he said.

Malaysia says it will send thousands of migrants and refugees back to Myanmar, despite acknowledging that many asylum seekers in the country had been victims of “atrocities” carried ​out by the junta in Naypyidaw.
The announcement comes just days after the UN’s highest court ruled Myanmar had committed genocide against its Rohingya minority.
Malaysia’s prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim, said on Tuesday that the deportations were in line with advice from the international court of justice (ICJ), which was “to guarantee a safe and dignified return” for those fleeing persecution, and his country had not abandoned its principles of upholding the rights of the people of Myanmar .
The UN has previously warned that migrants sent back to Myanmar could face a dangerous homecoming.
It is unclear how many Rohingya, a Muslim minority group, are among those facing deportation. However, the Rohingya make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, according to the UN. Many of the Rohingya escaped to Malaysia during a brutal military crackdown in 2017.
Anwar acknowledged that many asylum seekers in Malaysia were “victims of atrocities carried ​out by the Myanmar regime”, but said Malaysia could ‌no longer afford to host refugees. Hoping for them to be resettled in third countries had not worked, he said.
Many in Malaysia have grown increasingly frustrated by ‌the presence of refugees in the country, saying that hosting them has become a financial burden and a security risk, with a rise in anti-migrant sentiment in the country.
On Tuesday Anwar told Malaysia’s parliament that three naval ships would return 1,500 people in December, with an additional 5,303 people flown back by aircraft at the expense of the Myanmar government.
Tuesday’s announcement follows last week’s ICJ ruling in The Hague that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya.
The ICJ had never previously found a state responsible for genocide, and the judgment ended a seven-year legal battle that was seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.
The 2016-17 campaign by Myanmar’s military forced more than 700,000 mostly Muslim Rohingya to flee across the border into Bangladesh, arriving with reports of mass killings of adults and children, gang rapes and burnt-down villages.
In its judgment, the ICJ said Myanmar authorities must “allow and facilitate the safe, voluntary and dignified return” of refugees displaced either within Myanmar or abroad.
In September, Malaysia began sending back a group of about 1,500 Myanmar nationals as it launched its contested repatriation plan.
Malaysia’s government said in a statement at the time that the repatriation was necessary to resolve the “legacy issue” of foreign asylum seekers in Malaysia – of which it said 95% were from Myanmar.
“This long-standing issue has imposed a significant financial burden on the nation, triggered serious social crises, and created tangible security threats for the Malaysian people,” the statement said.
The UN had urged Malaysia to stop that repatriation, saying nobody should be deported to Myanmar, given the severity of the situation on the ground.
In late October, the Malaysian government said it would seek clarification from Myanmar over reports that hundreds of migrants recently returned were being held in military detention.

Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station when the latest crew blasts off Wednesday. Ali said he would be carrying "the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis" with him.
The first foreign astronaut on a Chinese space mission said on Tuesday that he will be carrying "the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis" when the latest crew blasts off on Wednesday.
Beijing has poured billions into the Chinese space programme, whose prized Tiangong space station is stewarded by teams of three astronauts that are typically rotated every six months.
The Shenzhou-24 mission is set to lift off at 8:18am (0018 GMT) on Wednesday from the Jiuquan launch centre in China's northwestern Gobi Desert, China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) spokesman Zhang Jingbo told a news conference on Tuesday.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani payload specialist, will become the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station.
"I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis," Ali told a separate news conference held later to introduce the crew.
"To every child who is watching while I'm in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams," he said in English, following other remarks in fluent Mandarin and Urdu.
Ali will join a short orbital flight expected to last around five days before returning with the Shenzhou-23 spaceship, which docked at the Tiangong in May.
Pakistani officials welcomed Ali's selection as a significant step in relations between Islamabad and Beijing.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the mission as a "source of joy and pride for the entire nation".
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the mission underscored the trust and "iron brotherhood" between the two countries.
Ali is not the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar explorer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023.
Beijing has invested heavily in its space programme in recent years, seeking to catch up with its principal rival , the United States.
Pakistan, which maintains close diplomatic and trade ties with Beijing, is a natural partner in the endeavour.
The crew currently aboard the Tiangong space station is headed by 40-year-old Zhu Yangzhu, Lai Ka-ying and Zhang Zhiyuan, also 40.
Lai is Hong Kong 's first astronaut and the only woman currently aboard the space station.
Watch more Conquering the far side of the Moon: Breaking down China's historic lunar mission
After the new, all-male crew reaches the Tiangong, Pakistan's Ali will return to Earth alongside Lai and Zhang.
Zhu will remain on board to complete China's first full-year stay in space – a key test of endurance critical for future lunar and potentially deep-space ambitions.
Zhu will be accompanied for the next six-month Tiangong rotation by 51-year-old space veteran Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, in his late thirties and making his first voyage to space.
Tang told reporters that learning to work together was more challenging in this mission, pointing to differences in language, culture and even psychology. But efforts from both sides have been paying off, Tang said.
“The labels and operating instructions aboard the spacecraft and space station are all in Chinese, and the Pakistani astronaut began training with virtually no foundation of the language," he said, adding that he and Wu also stepped up their English learning.
The Long March-2F rocket that will carry the crew into space will soon be filled with propellant, the CMSA's Zhang said.
The crew is in good condition and the space station is functioning normally, meeting all requirements for the mission, he said.

Fourteen countries from Europe, Africa and Oceania have acknowledged a landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, calling on the country to comply with its obligations under international law. The United Kingdom separately announced sanctions against five senior Myanmar military figures and said it would formally recognise the genocide.
The UK and 13 other countries on Monday "acknowledged" the top UN court's ruling that Myanmar perpetrated genocide against its Rohingya minority as London announced new sanctions.
The foreign ministers of Australia, Belgium, Canada, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Estonia, Iceland, Latvia, Luxembourg, New Zealand, Portugal, Spain, The Gambia and the United Kingdom said Myanmar had "violated its obligations under the Genocide Convention".
"We underscore that the Court's judgment is binding upon Myanmar and call on Myanmar to comply fully with its obligations under international law, including the Court's decision," they said in a joint statement.
The UK separately said it "formally recognises" genocide against the Rohingya and announced sanctions on five senior military figures.
"The horrific violence and persecution inflicted on the Rohingya cannot go unanswered," UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said.
The sanctions include asset freezes and travel bans, a Foreign Office statement said, adding that London "also intends to introduce legislation targeting the export and supply of aviation fuel to Myanmar".
"The UK is providing an additional £5m in new funding to support Rohingya and other communities with essential lifesaving and life-affirming services to approximately 350,000 people who need it most in Rakhine state, where humanitarian need is most acute," the statement added.
It said a further £3 million would "go towards strengthening accountability and justice for survivors of human rights abuses across Myanmar."
On November 19 in a historic verdict, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 crackdown in the western Rakhine state.
The ruling was the first time in the ICJ's 80-year history that it has determined that a state committed genocide.
Myanmar's government called the ruling unfair and a "great disappointment".
Shortly after the verdict, Britain announced it would expel Myanmar's defence attache.

Anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't.
The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi , co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders?
The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch.
Russia, which is currently engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes , has called it "a dangerous escalation".
It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism.
Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga.
Some of Ukraine's more audacious long-range drone attacks – what Zelensky likes to call "long-range sanctions" – have also struck targets thousands of kilometres beyond Ukraine's borders with Russia, deep inside Siberia.
The most notable of these was last year's Operation Spider's Web, which involved a specially adapted lorry that drove close to a Russian strategic nuclear bomber airbase and released a "swarm" of explosive drones that damaged or destroyed several expensive bombers.
And Ukraine has also been active further south in Africa where its forces have targeted Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps, the successor to the infamous Wagner Group that was accused of carrying out numerous human rights abuses.
It's not just Russia that will be alarmed by this latest Ukrainian operation in Benghazi harbour. The United Nations mission in Libya has already expressed its "deep concern".
Libyan officials point out that their country is not a party to the Russia-Ukraine war, although the Merkury and an accompanying cargo ship that was also hit were berthed in the eastern part of Libya controlled by the pro-Moscow warlord and self-styled "Field Marshal" Khalifa Haftar.
Throughout this year the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) has condemned all attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and today the global shipping community will be wondering whether this attack does indeed set a dangerous precedent.
If Ukraine can plan and execute such a bold attack on Russian ships in a nominally neutral harbour so far from home, where does this stop?
As the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches, this war has already been spreading, notably in other parts of Europe.
On Friday, several Russian projectiles landed well inside Poland's borders , just 60 miles from an Anglo-French exercise of forces intended to be deployed following an eventual ceasefire in Ukraine.
This, said Poland's PM Donald Tusk, was "a deliberate provocation" by Moscow.
It's not the first time Russian munitions have landed inside Poland, and therefore inside Nato territory, but observers have pointed out that Russia's probing of Nato's borders is becoming ever more brazen and some are calling for a firmer response.
But Russia is already heavily sanctioned by the West, with Europe having reduced much – but not all – of its energy imports from Russia, so the options for retaliation are limited, short of military confrontation, which no one wants.
Watch: CCTV shows explosion after Poland says airspace violated by Russian missile
Both Romania and Moldova have found themselves frequently struck by overflying Russian drones targeting Ukraine's Black Sea ports, while Bulgaria and Romania have suffered maritime drone attacks on commercial shipping just offshore in the Black Sea.
In the case of Romania, a Nato member, fast jets have had to be scrambled to intercept incoming Russian drones and there is a profound suspicion that these incursions are not all accidental.
The three Baltic states – Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania – all have borders with Russia and all consider themselves right on the front lines in this war.
There have been a number of anonymous attacks on military industrial facilities in these countries, blamed on agents acting on Moscow's behalf.
Russia, for its part, suspects Estonia of being complicit in Ukrainian drone attacks on the Baltic involving overflights through Estonian airspace.
It refers to the practice, by either side, of carrying out largely anonymous and unattributable operations using methods like cyber attacks, the burning down of warehouses supplying military equipment and the dispatching of drones, both for surveillance and loaded with explosives.
This autumn, Germany's Leipzig-Halle airport, which is used as a resupply hub by Ukraine's cargo aircraft, was targeted by three explosive drones that were discovered before anyone was hurt.
There have been other incidents involving explosive packages sent across Europe targeting Germany, Poland and the UK. Moscow denies any involvement.

Bangladesh's former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has said she plans to return home on 16 December, more than two years after a popular uprising forced her from power.
Hasina, who has lived in exile in Delhi since August 2024, has asked the Bangladeshi government to fly her back to Dhaka, her spokesperson said.
The announcement comes amid renewed unrest in Bangladesh, where supporters of her Awami League party have staged protests despite a ban on its activities.
But it's unclear how Hasina will return. Last year, a Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on student-led protests that ended her 15-year rule . She denies the charges.
Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kabir dismissed the prospect of Hasina returning on her own terms.
"Sheikh Hasina will not be able to return to the country as an ordinary commercial passenger; she will be brought back in handcuffs," he told a press briefing on Tuesday.
Kabir also accused Hasina and Delhi of fomenting recent unrest in Bangladesh, alleging that they were backing "terrorist activities" in the country.
India's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a ​request for comment. In April, ​the ministry said it was ⁠examining Bangladesh's request to extradite her and that it wanted to "engage constructively with the new government and further strengthen bilateral ties".
Hasina fled to India on 5 August 2024 as tens of thousands of protesters descended on Dhaka, and crowds stormed her official residence.
What began as student protests against quotas in government jobs turned into a mass uprising against her government following a deadly crackdown on demonstrators. The UN estimates that up to 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.
On Tuesday, Hasina's spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali accused Bangladeshi authorities of forcing her into exile in violation of the country's constitution.
"Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on 5 August 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," he said in a statement.
The choice of date is significant. Bangladesh celebrates Victory Day on 16 December, marking the end of its 1971 war of independence from Pakistan. Hasina's father, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, led the country's independence movement.
Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Hasina, described her decision as "deeply symbolic". "We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people," he said, expressing confidence that she would once again lead Bangladesh.
Hasina's announcement - and Dhaka's sharp response to it - come at a time when the ousted leader is seeking to reassert her political relevance from exile.
The Awami League was banned from political activities in May last year under the interim government led by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after Hasina's ouster.
The party was subsequently barred from contesting February's general election, which brought its long-time rival, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), to power, with Tarique Rahman becoming prime minister.
But the ban has not put an end to street protests by Awami League supporters, who have also called for nationwide shutdowns demanding Hasina's return.
Hasina, meanwhile, has repeatedly spoken of her desire to return to Bangladesh, even as she has acknowledged the risks of doing so.
"I know that they may put me in jail or they may kill me, anything may happen, but still I have to go back," she told a gathering of journalists in Delhi over an audio link in August, on the second anniversary of her ouster.
Hasina's continued political activities from Indian soil have also complicated Delhi's efforts to rebuild ties with Dhaka.
India enjoyed close relations with Hasina during her 15 years in power and had hoped that the election of a new government in Bangladesh would offer an opportunity to reset ties, which deteriorated sharply after her ouster.
But nine months after taking office, Rahman is yet to visit India despite an invitation. He has travelled to China, Japan and Malaysia, and skipped the BRICS summit hosted by India in September.
Discussions over a possible visit in August coincided with anger in Dhaka over Hasina's remarks to journalists in Delhi.
The two countries have since resumed talks about a visit, but no dates have been announced.

Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has become increasingly vocal about AI as end of term nears.
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called for measures to better manage the risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) during a conference in Barbados.
“Today I call for member states to coordinate efforts and to develop within the next year a globally inclusive and principles-based multilateral framework for AI risk management, backed by independent and credible oversight,” Guterres said Monday.
Guterres, who is approaching the end of his term due in December, has become increasingly vocal about the need for safety measures around advanced technology to avoid a future in which “ killer robots ” are a reality.
Guterres said Monday at the Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety that “when one looks at different other institutions of global governance … they correspond to the reality of the world in 1945”.
“It’s clear that institutions need to be reformed in order to adapt themselves to the realities of today’s world,” he said.
“That applies to the UN, and that applies to the international financial architecture, that applies to the world trade system.”
Guterres said that he would advise his successor, due to take office in the new year but yet to be selected, that properly controlling AI would be necessary for “humanity to maintain control of our world”.
International regulation of AI appears distant as the technology’s superpowers, the United States and China, continue to seek the upper hand in research and development breakthroughs.
Nonetheless, Guterres said that a starting point could be for countries to agree on shared safety measures, a testing regime and basic requirements for independent oversight.
In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX chief Elon Musk called for a slowdown in the development of AI.
Others, like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, want to move full steam ahead.
Regulators in the US, where AI development has proceeded at the fastest pace, appear unlikely to immediately intervene.
In September, US President Donald Trump hosted a group of American tech executives who agreed to abide by a voluntary code of conduct on AI safety.

Hasina urges Dhaka to arrange her return on the national airline, as government says she can only return through extradition.
Sheikh Hasina, the former prime minister of Bangladesh who was overthrown more than two years ago, plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, her spokesperson said, as the government said she can only return through extradition.
Hasina went into exile in August 2024 after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule.
She was later sentenced to death by a Bangladesh court in her absence for ordering the deadly crackdown on the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed.
Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready to fight the case once she is back.
Announcing her plan to return on the anniversary of the end of her country’s 1971 liberation war with Pakistan , she urged Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her flight on the national airline.
“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali said in a statement on Tuesday.
Abu Abdullah M Saleh, Prime Minister Rahman’s press secretary, told the Associated Press news agency that the government would stick to its position on Hasina’s extradition as a convict.
“My government’s stand is very clear. She has been convicted in a tribunal. We have sought her extradition,” he said by phone.
Hasina is expected to be arrested upon her return and sent to jail.
Aminul Islam, chief prosecutor of Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal, which sentenced Hasina to death, said it was unreasonable for a convicted fugitive to expect the government to arrange her return.
The judiciary had earlier said that Hasina would not be able to appeal her death sentence as she missed the required deadline and there would be no legal basis to stop her execution.
In Bangladesh, presidential clemency is allowed, but Hasina has never sought that in earlier statements and has rejected the verdict outright.
The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced Hasina from power.
Hasina’s father led the war against Pakistan and after independence was the first leader of the new People’s Republic of Bangladesh.
He was killed in a military coup in 1975, along with most of his family members. Hasina and her younger sister survived as they were out of the country.

Mexican officials say the United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help locate and capture one of the country's most wanted drug traffickers. The operation led to the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro'.
The United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help the government track down and capture a top drug lord over the weekend in Sinaloa, Mexican security officials said Monday.
The recent detention of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro” illustrates increasing law enforcement cooperation between the neighbouring countries, but US involvement in Mexican security operations has long been a touchy subject.
US President Donald Trump has pressured Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to crack down on cartels, while Mexico has repeatedly underscored its sovereignty . On Monday, Sheinbaum emphasized that US forces were not allowed to operate on the ground in Mexico and the governments were only sharing intelligence.
“This case in particular demonstrates the capacity of the armed forces” of Mexico to make major detentions, Sheinbaum said.
The US has sought to line up allies across Latin America to allow them to operate in their territories, with mixed responses from across the region.
The weekend detention of the capo, who was one of the FBI 's most wanted fugitives, triggered a burst of violence in the northern state of Sinaloa that left 20 people dead in the city of Guasave. Among them were four soldiers and 16 suspected criminals, Mexican officials said Monday.
Defense Secretary Gen. Ricardo Trevilla Trejo said Monday that the capture of Meza Flores and 16 members of his criminal group was the result of “very important intelligence sharing” with US authorities over the past three months to pinpoint Meza Flores’ location in Guasave.
In the week leading up to Meza Flores’ capture, that included authorizing the US to fly intelligence drones over Mexican territory, to assist Mexican law enforcement to later surround the capo and go in for the capture, Trevilla Trejo and other Mexican officials said. They emphasized that the intelligence mission was carried out in compliance with Mexican law.
Authorities also noted on Monday that the US had an existing extradition request for Meza Flores for drug trafficking charges, leaving open the possibility that the cartel boss may be sent north to face justice.
His capture was celebrated by Mexican and US law enforcement as a major blow to criminal groups in the region.
The US government highlighted its intelligence support in the operation, but did not immediately provide more details about the use of the surveillance drone when asked on Monday.
Meza Flores led the Beltran Leyva organization and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza Flores Transnational Criminal Organization. He was also a key ally of a Sinaloa Cartel faction known as “Los Mayos", which is locked in a brutal territorial war against another cartel faction in the Mexican state.
The capture of Meza Flores was the latest in a string of targeted operations against cartel kingpins by Mexican authorities, the largest of which was the February killing of Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes , known as " El Mencho ."
While the captures show that the government is doubling down on its fight on crime, many experts were quick to emphasize that the strategy could backfire.
In previous anti-crime offensives in Mexico and other parts of Latin America, knocking out cartel leaders without debilitating the entire criminal structure around them has largely only fueled bloody power struggles between cartel factions. That has been the case in recent years in Sinaloa.

UN chief Antonio Guterres on Monday urged countries to agree on the creation of a global framework for managing the dangers posed by artificial intelligence within one year. Speaking at a summit in Barbados, he warned that taming the technology is vital if humanity is to stay in charge of its own future.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called Monday for the world's nations to adopt a mechanism to temper the risks posed by AI , as he addressed a conference on the technology in Barbados .
As the end of Guterres's time at the helm of the international body approaches, he has become increasingly vocal about the need for AI safety measures to avoid a future in which " killer robots " are a reality.
Read more Nations agree to talks on regulating 'killer robots' by 2028
"Today I call for member states to coordinate efforts and to develop within the next year a globally inclusive and principles-based multilateral framework for AI risk management, backed by independent and credible oversight," he said.
International regulation of AI appears little more than a pipe dream as the technology's superpowers, the United States and China , seek the upper hand in research and development breakthroughs.
Nonetheless, Guterres said that a starting point could be for countries to agree on shared safety measures, a testing regime and basic requirements for independent oversight.
In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX chief Elon Musk called for a slowdown on the development of AI.
Read more AI leaders urge caution at UN, with Anthropic chief pledging to slow down
Others, like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg , want to move full steam ahead.
Regulators in the US, where AI development has proceeded at the fastest pace, are unlikely to intervene.
In September, US President Donald Trump hosted a group of American tech executives who agreed to abide by a voluntary code of conduct on AI safety.
Guterres said Monday at the Bridgetown Special Summit On AI Safety that "when one looks at different other institutions of global governance ... they correspond to the reality of the world in 1945."
"It's clear that institutions need to be reformed in order to adapt themselves to the realities of today's world," he said in response to an AFP question.
"That applies to the UN, and that applies to the international financial architecture, that applies to the world trade system."
Guterres said that he would advise his successor, due to take office in the New Year but yet to be selected, that properly controlling AI would be necessary for "humanity to maintain control of our world".

Muş 'un Korkut ilçesine 26 kilometre uzaklıktaki Kıryaka köyünde bulunan Türkan Akın Cerit İlkokulu'nda eğitim öğretim hayatı tek öğrenciyle devam ediyor. Yaklaşık 25 hanenin bulunduğu köyde yaşayan ikinci sınıf öğrencisi Seyit Zekeriya Aydın'ın eğitimi için Korkut İlçe Milli Eğitim Müdürlüğünce eğitim öğretim yılının başında ücretli öğretmen Gizem Uyanık görevlendirildi.
Köy okulunda görev yapan Uyanık, öğrencisinin eğitiminden geri kalmaması ve sosyal gelişimini sürdürebilmesi için derslerini birebir işliyor. Her sabah öğrencisi okula gelmeden önce odunları kırıp sobayı yakan fedakâr öğretmen, sınıfı ısıtarak ders için hazır hale getiriyor. Ders saatlerinde öğrencisine eğitim veren Uyanık, teneffüslerde ise onun oyun arkadaşı oluyor.
24 Kasım Öğretmenler Günü 'nde de öğrencisiyle birlikte okulda anlamlı bir gün yaşayan Uyanık'a, Seyit Zekeriya Aydın'dan sürpriz geldi. Annesinin özenle beslediği tavuklardan birini öğretmenine hediye eden küçük öğrencinin bu jesti, Gizem Öğretmeni mutlu etti.
Tek öğrencisini geleceğe hazırlamak için her gün aynı özveriyle çalışan öğretmen Gizem Uyanık, "Bütün öğretmenlerimizin, tüm meslektaşlarımın Öğretmenler Günü'nü kutluyorum. Kıryaka köyündeki tek öğretmenli okulda görev yapıyorum. Zekeriya hem bu okulun tek öğrencisi hem de bu köyün tek çocuğu. Başka bir arkadaşı yok. Ben hem okulda ders veriyorum hem de dışarıda onunla oyun oynuyorum. Aynı zamanda onu geleceğe hazırlayan bir pusula olmaya çalışıyorum. O da bu konuda bana çok yardımcı oluyor. Çok uslu bir çocuk.
İlk defa Öğretmenler Günü'nü kutladım. İlk öğretmenlik tecrübem. Zekeriya ve ailesi bana sürpriz paketler yerine bir tavuk almıştı. Tavuğu getirip hediye etti. Çok mutlu oldum, benim için çok farklı ve güzel bir sürpriz oldu. Artık okulda üç kişiyiz; ben, Zekeriya ve tavuğumuz. İnşallah Zekeriya ve tavuğumuzla bundan sonra birlikte daha çok oyun oynayacağız. Tüm öğretmenlerimizin Öğretmenler Günü'nü kutluyorum" dedi.
Köyün tek çocuğu ve okulun tek öğrencisi olan Seyit Zekeriya Aydın ise "Bugün Öğretmenler Günü. Hediye olarak öğretmenime tavuk getirdim. Öğretmenimi çok seviyorum" diye konuştu.

Alevlerin içinden sağ çıkan Alya, aynı zamanda içinde taşıdığı en büyük sırrın ağırlığıyla da baş etmek zorundadır. Hayatını kurtaran gizemli adam Kartal Varlıer, Albora'nın kapısından içeri adım atar. Alya ve Cihan bu yangının bir kaza olmadığından emindir. Gölgede kalan adamı bulup yüzüne bakacağına yemin eder. Cihan, ölümden döndüğü gecenin sabahında kalbini artık saklamamaya karar verir. Bir yüzük, bir söz ve hâlâ cevap bekleyen bir soru, Alya ile Cihan'ı yeniden aynı eşiğe getirir.
Cihan’ın karşısındaki görünmeyen güç, Albora’yı bu kez iki ayrı cephede hedef alır: Kaya sınırda kurulan pusunun içine çekilirken Yonca Hastanesi sabotajla karanlığa gömülür. Hastanede hayati tehlikeyle karşı karşıya kalan Nare’yi hiç beklenmedik biri kurtarırken, Zerrin ise Kaya’yı korumak için kendi güvenliğini hiçe sayacaktır.
Albora’nın geleceğine dair düşünceleri kararını ağırlaştırırken, İpek’in DNA kağıdını bulup Cihan’ın eline vermesi, Sadakat’in koruduğu bu büyük sırrı artık gizli kalamayacak bir noktaya taşır. Konakta ise Sadakat, kırk yıllık hayatını sarsan bir gerçekle yüzleşir. Söylemekle susmak arasında kalan Sadakat'in her suskunluğu, konaktaki herkesi biraz daha tedirgin eder. DNA sonucuyla yüzleşen Sadakat, Cihan’la ilgili yıllardır sakladığı gerçeği açıklamakla onu kaybetmek arasında kalır.

Pazartesi akşamı Kanal D 'de Uzak Şehir , ATV 'de Altı Üstü İstanbul , TRT 1'de ise Evlilik Güzeldir ekran başındakilerin karşısına çıktı. Bir süredir final iddialarıyla anılan TRT 1 dizisi TOTAL, AB ve ABC1 listelerinin üçünde de geçen haftanın üzerine çıkarken, zirveyi kimseye bırakmayan Uzak Şehir çift haneli reytinge sadece 0,04 puan uzakta kaldı. 23 Kasım Pazartesi reyting sonuçları belli oldu.
TRT 1'in pazartesi dizisi Evlilik Güzeldir, ekim ayında reytinglerin gerilemesiyle birlikte final iddialarının odağına yerleşmişti ve o günden bu yana her yeni bölümün rakamları sosyal medyada büyüteçle inceleniyor. Gazeteci Birsen Altuntaş bu iddialar üzerine 'Final durumu yok, devam ediyor şu an' demiş, dizi de İzmir Aliağa'daki fabrika patlaması nedeniyle yayından kaldırılan 9 Kasım bölümünün ardından 16 Kasım'da 10. bölümüyle ekrana dönmüştü. O akşam TOTAL'de 2,25 alarak 13. sırada kalan dizi, 23 Kasım'daki 11. bölümüyle 2,74'e çıkıp 11. sıraya yükseldi ve geçen haftaya göre 0,49 puan kazandı.
Asıl sıçrama ise AB 'de geldi. Dizi bu listede 2,71'den 3,71'e çıkarak tam 1,00 puan artırdı, 7. sıradan 5. sıraya tırmandı ve 2 Kasım'daki 9. bölümün aldığı 3,19'u da geride bıraktı. ABC1'de 3,39 ile 9. sırada yer alan yapım, bu listede de bir önceki haftanın üzerine çıkmayı başardı.
Evlilik Güzeldir'in listelerdeki bu toparlanışı dikkat çekse de pazartesi akşamının zirvesindeki isim bu hafta da değişmedi. Uzak Şehir , 9 Kasım'da 10,10 ile çift haneyi gördükten sonra 16 Kasım'da 9,79'a gerilemiş, bir reyting uzmanı da bu düşüşü ara tatil haftasına bağlayıp rakamların bir sonraki hafta dengeye geleceğini söylemişti. Mahamadou Diaby, yöresel kıyafetleri ve Erzurum şivesiyle dikkat çekiyor.
Mali'den üniversite eğitimi için Erzurum 'a gelen 22 yaşındaki Mahamadou Diaby, 4 yılda Dadaş kültürünü benimsedi. Erzurum şivesiyle konuşup kıtlama çay içmeye başlayan Diaby samimi tavırları ve yöreye olan ilgisiyle görenlerin dikkatini çekiyor.
Batı Afrika ülkesi Mali'den 2022 yılında üniversite eğitimi için 9 bin 418 kilometre uzaklıktaki Erzurum'a gelen Diaby, aradan geçen 4 yılda kentin kültürüne ve yaşam tarzına uyum sağlayarak adeta bir Dadaş oldu.
Atatürk Üniversitesi Mühendislik Fakültesi Elektrik-Elektronik Mühendisliği Bölümü öğrencisi olan Diaby, kendisini Dadaş olarak tanımlıyor, yöresel kıyafetlerden potur giyiyor ve Erzurum ağzıyla konuşuyor. Kahvehanelere giderek vatandaşlarla sohbet eden Diaby, samimi tavırları ve yöreye olan ilgisiyle görenlerin dikkatini çekiyor.
Günlük konuşmalarında kullandığı yöresel ifadelerle çevresindekileri şaşırtan genç öğrenci , kıtlama ve limonlu çay içerek de Erzurum kültürünü yaşatıyor.
Mali'den Erzurum'a eğitim için geldiğini ve geçen 4 yılda kente alıştığını belirten Mahamadou Diaby, "4 yıl oldu Erzurum'a geleli. 7 yıl dolduktan sonra zaten Erzurumlu olacağım. Dadaşlar candır. Mesela ‘Senin canın yiyim' en sevdiğim ifadelerden birisidir. ‘Senin canın yiyim, gardaş, neyedisen' tarzı ifadelerle konuşulur burada. Sevdim, Erzurum'a alıştım. İçlik (potur) giyiyorum mesela. Giyiyorum ama çok soğuk. Yapacak bir şey yok, alıştım buraya. Mali'den sonra buranın iklimi biraz farklı geldi. Ama alıştık diyebilirim. Dadaş üşümüyor zaten biliyorsun. Erzurum'u herkese öneriyorum. Gelin buraya, kıtlama şekeri var, limonsuz çay içilmez. Çok eğlenceli, çok kültürel bir yer. Erzurum'u tanıtmak istersem; kar, beyaz, insanları sıcakkanlı, kısaca karı-kışı Dadaşı. Dadaş üşümez. Burada çayı da kıtlama içerim" dedi.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c65y:
The first ever Children's Booker Prize has announced the eight books in the running for the new £50,000 award.
Five novels, two graphic novels and an illustrated collection of short stories are on the shortlist, which is aimed at children aged eight to 12.
The authors in contention include former Children's Laureate of Ireland Eoin Colfer, who is best known for his Artemis Fowl series, and teacher and children's author Catherine Bruton.
Four children have also been announced as new judges after a UK-wide competition. Twelve-year-old Ibrahim from Hampshire was one of those picked from more than 4,000 entrants.
He told me he was called back into school for a phone call with chair of judges Frank Cottrell-Boyce, who broke the news. Ibrahim said he couldn't be happier.
"First Children's Booker Prize judge! On my CV - that's going to take me a long way… I'm too overwhelmed to even be excited."
Cottrell-Boyce told the BBC "it's really, really important that this is a prize for children's books. Having judges who are children will be proof of that… If the children don't love a book, it won't win."
Ibrahim, his fellow child judges and Cottrell-Boyce will be joined on the judging panel by Ghosts and Horrible Histories actor Lolly Adefope and Sanchita Basu De Sarkar, who owns an award-winning children's book shop in north London.
Ibrahim said he loves reading "because it's just a way to unwind yourself from the outside world. If you get stuck in a book, you're not getting your face out of there until you finish it".
He's far too professional to share which books on the list he likes best, but he told me when he was reading one of them recently: "I had to tell my mum to confiscate it because I couldn't stop reading it and I was getting a headache."
Cottrell-Boyce said he isn't concerned over whether the adult judges might dominate the decision-making.
"If - like me - you've been visiting schools as a children's writer for 20 years, it's a rare thing to meet a child who is too over-awed to express an opinion. They're usually very forthright".
Ibrahim proves that point. He told me "the adults are not going to control that meeting… 100% not!"
He's looking for "something that has different perspectives, you can see it in a different way. New characters, not just the same old sloppy characters that authors make all the time. They just make these books that just have the same plot line".
The shortlisted books are by authors from the UK, Ireland, Australia, Italy and Pakistan. Cottrell-Boyce described the list as "full of surprises." Here it is:
The Worst Thing That Could Possibly Happen by Guy Bass, illustrated by David Roberts. Readers on Goodreads describe it as "super creepy" and "how horror for kids should be written."
War by Eoin Colfer and Andrew Donkin, illustrated by Giovanni Rigano. It's the third book in their graphic novel series and tells the story of 14-year old Kat, living under siege in an unnamed European city.
The Night I Borrowed Time by Iqbal Hussain - the British-Pakistani author and former journalist's debut Children's book weaves a story through the eyes of Zubair, a seventh son who has inherited the power of time travel and tries to fix the lives of his family.
The Rambler's Curse by Mikey Please - the fantasy-comedy by the Aardman animator, who has also illustrated the book, has been described by The Guardian as a "laugh-out-loud, shaggy-dog spiral of purposes mistook".
The Teller of Tall Tales by Liz Hyder, illustrated by Tom de Freston, was a critic's choice in The Daily Telegraph. It's about a grandmother living in a remote cabin who weaves mysterious stories for her estranged grandson.
Tadpole Summer by Catherine Bruton is about a frog whose younger brother is unwell. It's described as a song to nature, family and friendship
Séamus Almost Famous by Jessica Scott-Whyte - this is the Irish author's second book and is illustrated by Becka Moor. Poor Séamus is on a mission to emerge from the shadows of his family - even his baby sister is an accidental internet sensation.
Hometown by Australian Shaun Tan tells the story of a girl living on a distant planet who is one day told by a visitor in a spacesuit that she is actually from somewhere very far away. A review in The Observer called it "perfect fuel for a voracious imagination".
Cottrell-Boyce told the BBC the range of subjects was "amazing".
"Children's books can be about anything, can deal with anything. But the tone has to convey hope. I can't think of a darker childhood than the one endured by Anne of Green Gables. I also can't think of a more joyous book than Anne of Green Gables."
He acknowledges the worrying statistics on reading. The National Literacy Trust's Annual Literacy Survey last year showed the percentage of children and young people who said they enjoyed reading was its lowest in 20 years. Just one in three aged eight to 18 said they enjoyed reading in their free time, down by more than a third since 2005.
"That's why we're here! To fight the fight. To make sure our children have as many opportunities as possible to discover how pleasurable, how bonding, how thrilling and enriching and fortifying it can be to slip out of the prison of the present into the infinity of the story."
He doesn't try to persuade them. "I let them live their life. I live my life".
"Put a timer on your phone, make sure it's blocked and then they'll decide to do something more productive. I might be able to convince them... because it can help you with English, your confidence, and help you build self esteem."
For him, though, the best thing about a book is when it takes him into another world. "If you try to take your head out of it, it makes you think 'oh my god what's going to happen next?'"
The winning book will be announced in February next year at the Young V&A in London. 30,000 copies of the shortlisted books will be given to children who need them most.

Doğuştan bedensel engelli 45 yaşındaki Mustafa Alkan, öğrenci olarak girdiği okulun öğretmeni oldu.
Gaziantep 'in Şahinbey ilçesinde bulunan Vehbi Dai İlkokulu'ndan 1994 yılında mezun olan ve lise yıllarında öğretmeninden aldığı ilhamla öğretmen olmaya karar veren 45 yaşındaki Mustafa Alkan, öğretmenlik hayalini gerçekleştirmek için 2005 yılında Malatya İnönü Üniversitesi Sınıf Öğretmenliği Bölümü'nde dört yıllık eğitim aldı.
Eğitimini başarıyla tamamlayan Alkan, mezuniyetinin ardından girdiği KPSS sınavını kazanarak öğretmenlik mesleğine adım attı.
Türkiye 'nin çeşitli illerinde bedensel engelinin getirdiği zorluklara rağmen pes etmeyerek görev yapan ve öğretmenlik hayalini gerçekleştiren Alkan, daha sonra ise 1994 yılında mezun olduğu Vehbi Dai ilkokuluna atandı.
Yıllarca çocukluğunun geçtiği okulda öğrencilerini geleceğe hazırlayan Alkan, bir zamanlar öğrenci olduğu okulda öğretmen olarak görev yapmanın ve öğrenci yetiştirmenin gururunu yaşıyor.
Mustafa Alkan, mezuniyetinin ardından girdiği KPSS sınavını kazanarak öğretmenlik mesleğine adım attı.
“BU OKULA ÖĞRENCİ OLARAK GELMİŞTİM ŞİMDİ ÖĞRETMENLİK YAPIYORUM”
Öğrenci olarak geldiği okulda öğretmenlik yapmanın gururunu yaşadığını ifade eden Mustafa Alkan, "Vehbi Dai İlkokulu'nda öğretmenlik yapıyorum. Mesleğimin 21. yılı. İlkokula 1989 yılında kayıt yaptırdım. 1994'te mezun oldum ve 2011'de burada göreve başladım. Çok güzel bir duygu. Gerçekten buraya öğrenci olarak geldik, şimdi öğretmenlik yapıyoruz. Bize katkı sağlayan öğretmenlerimize teşekkür ediyoruz. Biz de aynı katkıyı çocuklarımıza, öğrencilerimize sağlamaya çalışıyoruz. Öğretmenlik açıkçası bir yaşam tarzı. Birilerine bir şey katmak, bir eğitim vermek. Küçük çocukları sıfırdan alıp yeni yoğrulacak bir hamur gibi yoğurmak, büyütmek, geliştirmek ve ileride bir yerlere geldiğini görmek insana gerçekten mutluluk veriyor. Çok özel bir duygu. Yani anlatmakta zorlanıyoruz gerçekten" dedi.
İlk görev yerine ilişkin de konuşan Alkan, ilk yıllarında bedensel engelinden dolayı zorlandığını aktararak, "İlk göreve başladığım okul bir dağ köyündeydi. Özellikle şartları zorluydu. Okula gidip gelmek biraz sorun oluyordu. Köy okulunda lojman da biraz sıkıntılıydı. O konuda birazcık zorlandım. Bir de göreve ilk başlama esnasında tek öğretmen olarak bir okula gittiğiniz zaman ister istemez acemilik çekiyorsunuz. Ama fiziksel olarak gerçekten dağ köyü benim için zor oluyordu" ifadelerini kullandı.
Alkan, bir zamanlar öğrenci olduğu okulda öğretmen olarak görev yapmanın ve öğrenci yetiştirmenin gururunu yaşıyor.
Görev yaptığı okulda fiziki şartlar açısından herhangi bir sorun yaşamadığını belirten Alkan, "Genel olarak idaremiz fiziki şartlarda bana yardımcı oluyor. Asansörümüz var mesela, sınıfa çıkarken asansörü kullanabiliyorum. Sınıfta genel olarak pek bir sorun yaşamıyoruz. Öğrencilerimizle iletişimimiz iyi, materyallere ulaşımımız kolay. Akıllı tahtalar çok büyük kolaylık sağladı. Yani emeği geçenlere teşekkürler. Burada kendim ilkokulu okudum dedim ya ilk başta. Bu benim için büyük bir deneyim. Çünkü bu sosyal çevrenin, bu ortamın sosyoekonomik durumunu biliyorum. Öğrencilerin durumunu biliyorum. Bundan dolayı empati kurmakta hiç zorlanmıyorum. Yani çok bir sorun yaşamıyoruz" diye konuştu.
“DAHA ÖNCE ÖĞRENCİ OLDUĞUM BİR OKULDA ÖĞRETMENLİK YAPMAK FARKLI BİR DENEYİM”
Mezun olduğu okulda öğretmenlik yapmanın kendisine önemli kolaylıklar sağladığını dile getiren Alkan, "İlkokulu okuduğun okulda öğretmenlik yapmak farklı bir deneyim ama farklı kolaylıkları da var. Çünkü çevreyi biliyorsun, velileri biliyorsun, ortamı biliyorsun, okulu biliyorsun, her şeyi biliyorsun. Yani çok büyük kolaylığı oluyor bu konuda. Öğretmenliğin tüm hatıraları özel. Her bir öğrencinin gelip size sarılmasından hiçbir çıkar gözetmeden sizi sevdiğini anlıyorsunuz. O bakışından veya herhangi bir hareketinden size verdiği değeri, size olan sevgisini anlıyorsunuz. Şurası daha özel diyebileceğiniz bir an yok. Bizim için her an özel" şeklinde konuştu.
24 Kasım Öğretmenler Günü dolayısıyla meslektaşlarının gününü de kutlayan Alkan, “Tüm öğretmen arkadaşların Öğretmenler Günü'nü şimdiden kutluyorum. İnşallah mesleğimize gereken önem verilir. Öğretmen artık sadece derse girip dersi anlatıp çıkan bir kişiye dönüştürüldü. Biz tüm çocuklarımızı, tüm öğrencilerimizi kendi çocuklarımızdan ayırt etmeden eğitmek istiyoruz. Yeri geldiğinde öğrencimize ”Dur yavrum, yapma kızım, yapma oğlum' diyebilmek istiyoruz" ifadelerine yer verdi.

Başvurduğu bir bankadan 1 milyon 500 bin TL’lik kredi çekip 10 gebe büyükbaş hayvan satın aldı. Bu uğurda otomobilini de satıp çiftliğine traktör ve ekipmanlar kattı. Saman balyalarının arasına yumurtlayan tavuk, kaz ve hindi gibi çok sayıda kanatlı hayvanın da bulunduğu çiftliğinde her gün 1,5 yaşındaki gebe düvelerinin yemlerinin hazırlanması ile ahırın temizliğini kendisi yapıp doğumları için gün sayan 35 yaşındaki Orak, "Eşim ve arkadaşlarımın desteğiyle ahır inşa edildi. Her köşesinde emeğimiz var. Köye de taşındım. Sabah akşam hayvanlarımın yanındayım. 'Muallime Hanımın Çiftliği'nde keyifler yerinde. Kredi ödemesine iki yıl sonra başlayacağım. 5 yıllık ödeme planı var. Ben garanticiyim. Doğumlarla aramıza katılacak buzağıları bile satsam borcumu kapatmış olurum" diye konuştu.
Hayvanları için kaba yem ihtiyacını arazisinden karşılamanın planlarını da yapan Orak, "Ben de kamuya atanamadım. Ama yılmadım. Özel sektörde çalıştım. Şimdi de hayallerimin peşinde koşuyorum. Bir kadına, gence ilham olabilirsem çok mutlu olurum. Onlara ‘haydi gelin, köyümüze geri dönelim’ diyorum. Hedeflerim büyük. Muallime hanım olarak küçük bir çiftlik kurdum. Ama ilerleyen süreçte büyük bir çiftliğin kapılarını öğrencilerime açmak istiyorum. Üretim sahası kurarak gezen çocukların sütün nasıl sağıldığını, yoğurdun nasıl yapıldığını görmelerini istiyorum" şeklinde konuştu.

Yargıtay 9. Hukuk Dairesi, işverenin aracıyla başka bir firmanın yetkilisini toplantılara götüren ve izinsiz rezervasyon yaptıran kimya mühendisinin işten çıkarılmasını haklı fesih saydı. Aynı şirkette 5 yıl çalışan mühendis, kıdem ve ihbar tazminatı alamayacak. Kararda, sadakat borcunun ihlali için işçinin maddi menfaat sağlamış olmasının şart olmadığı da vurgulandı.
Bir şirkette beş yıl boyunca çalışan kimya mühendisi, başka bir firmanın işleriyle ilgilendiği iddiasıyla işten çıkarıldı. Mühendis, işverenle ücret artışlarından doğan farkların ödenmemesi yüzünden gerginlik yaşadıklarını, feshin haksız olduğunu savunarak İş Mahkemesi'ne başvurdu ve ücret alacaklarının tahsilini istedi.
İşveren ise mühendisin sadakat yükümlülüğünü ihlal ettiğini öne sürüp davanın reddini talep etti. İş Mahkemesi davayı kısmen kabul etti. Mahkeme, bir menfaat elde edildiğinin ispatlanamadığını belirterek fesihte haklı neden bulunmadığı, ancak geçerli bir fesih nedeni olduğu sonucuna vardı. İşveren vekilleri kararı istinafa taşıdı, Bölge Adliye Mahkemesi başvuruyu esastan reddetti. Dosya, işverenin temyiziyle Yargıtay 9. Hukuk Dairesi'ne geldi.
Yargıtay 'ın dikkat çektiği ilk olay, mühendisin işverenin anlaşmalı olduğu bir otelde yaptırdığı rezervasyondu. Davacı, başka bir firmanın yetkilisi adına oda ayırttı. Üstelik bunu işyeri yöneticilerine bilgi vermeden ve onlardan izin almadan yaptı.
Daire kararında, mühendisin benzer sektörde faaliyet gösteren başka bir şirketin yetkilisi için toplantılar da organize ettiğini kaydetti.
Dosyadaki delillere göre mühendis, izinli olduğu dönemde işverene ait aracı kullandı ve başka şirketin yetkilisini hem şehir içi hem şehirlerarası toplantılara götürdü. Yargıtay bu durumun sabit olduğunu kaydetti.
Dairenin değerlendirmesinde bu davranışlar doğruluk kurallarıyla bağdaşmıyordu. Karara göre rezervasyon ve araç kullanımı birlikte ele alındığında ortaya çıkan tablo, işveren açısından haklı fesih nedeni oluşturuyordu.
Emsal niteliği taşıyan kısım tam burada: Yargıtay 9. Hukuk Dairesi, fesih nedeninin kabulü için işçinin mutlaka maddi menfaat sağlamış olmasının gerekmediğini belirtti. İş Mahkemesi'nin ilk derecede dayandığı 'menfaat ispatlanamadı' gerekçesi bu noktada yeterli görülmedi.
Daire, işverenin fesihte haklı olduğu sonucuna ulaştı. Davacı lehine kıdem ve ihbar tazminatına hükmedilmesini ise hukuka aykırı buldu. Yani 5 yıllık çalışmanın ardından mühendisin eline bu iki tazminattan hiçbiri geçmeyecek.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck3r:
US rapper Don Toliver has postponed two shows in London this week, after his concert in Manchester on Sunday was evacuated when an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd.
Toliver was due to play The O2 on Monday and Wembley Arena on Tuesday, but Live Nation said his "stage and production equipment remains in Manchester and cannot be moved in time".
One person was taken to hospital and 89 people showed "symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure" after Sunday's Co-op Live arena show, police said.
Fans described "distressing scenes" with people "choking", "screaming" and "coughing up blood" because of the effects of a substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas.
Watch: Coughs, confusion and boos as Co-op Live concert cancelled
The Wembley show has been rescheduled to 14 December, while Monday night's O2 gig has been moved to 15 December.
"I'm very sad to sit here and say I have to reschedule The O2 London show to December 15th due to (the) unfortunate incident last night," Don Toliver wrote on Instagram.
Greater Manchester Police (GMP) declared a major incident on Sunday and said 12,000 people were evacuated from the arena.
One woman was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further assessment and treatment after the incident, which happened at about 22:00 GMT, the force said.
A further 88 people "underwent dry decontamination at the scene and were subsequently accommodated within the Etihad Stadium while the incident was managed", according to GMP.
Leon Douzi said he was right next to where the substance was released, and described someone holding a can and "this gas coming out".
"It just hit me in the throat," he said, adding that it felt like "burning".
There was "a bit of panic", Douzi said: "Everybody was having the same feeling and trying to get out."
Some fans reported eye and respiratory symptoms, according to the North West Ambulance Service.
Hannah Baxter, who went to the concert with her partner, said the first thing she noticed was a burning feeling in her throat.
"[We] were just coughing and coughing... there was a guy next to us who had vomited. There were people with red eyes and... tears everywhere," she told the BBC.
Joey Howe, a football journalist at the gig, told BBC Radio Manchester there was a "horrible smell" and added: "People were coming through in wheelchairs choking – it was really distressing."
Police launched an investigation and are continuing to carry out tests on items at the venue to try to identify the substance. No arrests have been made.
Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said: "Enquiries remain ongoing to establish the nature of the substance, where it came from and any associated risk. Testing will take place throughout the day as the investigation into the cause of this incident progresses.
"We are trying to establish whether any criminality has occurred in relation to this incident."
Some fans complained about security and a lack of searches as people went into the Manchester concert.
Jessica Moult-Boffey, of Wigan, said people were "crying and screaming in pain" as they left the venue, adding she felt "confused on how something like that got into a venue of that size".
Malachi Clarke also claimed security was "not good at all", adding: "They weren't checking bags, to the point where I had to ask them if they needed to check mine."
Co-op Live said on its website there were a range of security measures, and while "some of these are visible, others you won't be able to see".
It said the arena used a "frictionless security screening that detects prohibited items without you needing to empty your pockets".
Figen Murray, the mother of a Manchester Arena attack victim who led the campaign for a new law to prevent terrorist attacks at public venues, said people should feel "assured" about security measures.
"A lot of the big venues use mass screening technology, where you don't even know you've been checked," she told the BBC. They also have staff observing CCTV, security guards and plain-clothed officers on site.
Murray said that while the current technology is "good enough", it needed improvement over the next few years to become "more sophisticated".
Venues are currently focused on keeping out items – such as explosives – that could cause mass casualties, she added.
Police investigate unknown substance that caused Manchester's Co-op Live evacuation
'People were screaming in pain' during Co-op Live evacuation
All fans at the Manchester show will get a full refund, promoter Live Nation said.
A statement said: "We are sorry to everyone affected by last night's events in Manchester and full refunds for that show will be automatically processed to ticket holders."
There have apparently been similar incidents earlier on Toliver's tour, when some fans reported spray or gas being released into the crowd in Zurich and Paris.
In his post on Monday, the rapper said: "I just wanna make sure everyone is safe and the next show goes on properly. My heart and prayers are with everyone that was injured last night."
"The only thing I love more than creating music is performing for my fans," Toliver said, asking people to stop bringing substances into his shows.
"It ain't cool," added the rapper, who was nominated for five Grammy Awards earlier this month. "See you soon London, love you Guys. DT."
Toliver's Wembley Arena appearance on Tuesday was set to be the last gig of his world tour before he took a break from the road ahead of a Coachella appearance next spring.
Toliver is best known for singles such as No Idea and After Party, from his debut studio album, Heaven or Hell (2020), which was big on TikTok. He also featured on Travis Scott's song Can't Say, from his third studio album Astroworld.

Roman müziğinin en renkli isimlerinden Kobra Murat, oğlu Yiğithan'ın nişanı için ailesiyle birlikte gelin evine gitti. Müstakbel gelin kapıyı açar açmaz cebinden bir tomar dolar çıkaran Murat, paraları gelinin üstüne saçtı. 'Dolarlı yaşa babam, altınlara basacaksın' diyerek gelinine bolluk dileyen ünlü isim, daha önce kızının nişanında da euro ve dolar yağdırmıştı.
Gerçek adı Murat Divandiler olan, İstanbul Balat'ta yaşayan ve terzilik yapan Kobra Murat'ın oğlu Yiğithan, evlilik yolunda ilk adımı attı. Nişan için ailesiyle birlikte gelin evine giden Kobra Murat, kapıda eğlenceli anlar yaşadı.
Müstakbel gelin kapıyı açtığı anda Murat cebinden bir tomar dolar çıkardı ve paraları gelinin üstüne saçtı. O anlar, nişana ait görüntülere de yansıdı. Paranın tutarı ve nişanın yapıldığı yer ise paylaşılmadı.
Kobra Murat, dolarları saçarken gelinine dualarla dolu bir karşılama yaptı.
'Dolarlı yaşa babam, altınlara basacaksın babam, yazlıkların kışlıkların olacak. Paşa gibi kocayı kapmışsın' diyen Murat, yeni gelinine bolluk içinde bir hayat diledi.
Kobra Murat, 'paşa gibi koca' benzetmesiyle oğlu Yiğithan'ı da övmeyi ihmal etmedi. Ünlü ismin altına, yazlığa ve kışlığa uzanan iyi dilekleri, onun alışılmış gösterişli tarzını bir kez daha ortaya koydu.
Kobra Murat'ın 'azı değil, fazlası' anlayışı ilk kez gündeme gelmiyor.
Daha önce kızı için düzenlediği nişan töreninde takılan altınlar, havada uçuşan eurolar ve dolarlar sosyal medyada uzun süre tartışılmıştı. Ünlü ismin altın kaplama detaylarla süslü 5 katlı evi de defalarca gündem olmuştu. Daha önce Evrim Akın'ın da ziyaret ettiği evin kapısındaki el yazısıyla 'Kobra' yazısı ve garajda boydan boya asılı fotoğrafı da çok konuşulmuştu.
Öte yandan Kobra Murat, yalnızca bir hafta önce sağlık sorunlarını anlatmıştı. 'Çok kötüyüm yavrum. 13 tane ameliyatlıyım, çok yoruluyorum' diyen Murat, sevenlerinden dua istemiş, torununun evlendiğini görmek istediğini söylemişti. Sanatçı, Aralık 2023 'te de bağırsak çatlağı nedeniyle acil ameliyata alınmıştı.
Eylül ayında ise yabancı numaralardan tehdit mesajları aldığını, kendisinden 1 milyon dolar istendiğini açıklayarak suç duyurusunda bulunmuştu. Zorlu geçen ayların ardından Kobra Murat'ın yüzü bu kez oğlunun nişanıyla güldü.
